trigger_events.description: An emission or release record has been captured at an establishment and is available for corporate sustainability disclosure.

handoffs.description: A logged safety incident feeds the health-and-safety metrics that corporate sustainability disclosure reports against (recordable rates, lost-time injuries).

trigger_events.description: A new safety incident, injury, illness, or near-miss has been reported and enters investigation. Downstream: feeds recordkeeping and corporate sustainability incident metrics.

handoffs.description: Carrier reconciliation exceptions become HR-cases for impacted employees. Alert-without-feedback-loop friction shape.

trigger_events.description: Carrier acknowledgment processed; discrepancies flagged. BEN-ADMIN owns remediation; HRSD case may open for affected employees.

handoffs.description: Sustained low-engagement signal opens an HR case for manager outreach and follow-up.

trigger_events.description: Engagement driver score declined materially vs the prior cycle. EMP-EXP and TALENT-MGMT triage; HRSD may open a manager-outreach case.

handoffs.description: HR service delivery picks up new HR knowledge articles for employee self-service.

trigger_events.description: A KB article is published; CSM, HRSD, agent assist, and conversational AI receive content updates.

handoffs.description: When an onboarding task is blocked, overdue, or contested (missing document, declined accommodation, pre-boarding question), an HR case is opened in HRSD. HRSD masters the case lifecycle; the case-resolution event flows back to unblock the task. Friction comes from inconsistent case-routing taxonomies between Onboarding and HRSD.

trigger_events.description: Fired when a Onboarding Task is escalation required. Publisher domain owns the state transition; subscribers may react by creating downstream artifacts.

handoffs.description: Access-related HR questions can spawn HRSD cases for context.

trigger_events.description: Access request raised (joiner provisioning, mover entitlement change, ad-hoc). Approval workflow starts; SoD pre-check evaluates.

handoffs.description: Statement issuance creates predictable spike of worker questions; HRSD pre-stages KB and case intake.

trigger_events.description: Personalized total-rewards statement generated and delivered. EMP-EXP captures engagement; HRSD answers questions.

handoffs.description: Adverse-action workflow requires HR-legal review; manual escalation common. Friction shape: alert/escalation without feedback loop.

trigger_events.description: Background-check returned with adjudication-required findings. Offer may be rescinded; legal/HR review required.

handoffs.description: HR Service Delivery opens (or updates) an employee-facing case/task with the impending obligation, deadline, and link to the assigned course. Failure mode: when an HRSD platform isn't deployed, the nudge falls back to direct email and the in-tool reminder.

trigger_events.description: Mandatory compliance training nearing/at due date. HRSD and HCM nudge employee + manager; GRC tracks obligation status.

handoffs.description: Termination kicks off offboarding case (exit interview, knowledge transfer, paperwork). Multiple downstream HRSD tasks created.

trigger_events.description: Fired when a Employee is terminated. Publisher domain owns the state transition; subscribers may react by creating downstream artifacts.

handoffs.description: No-show triggers HRSD case for attendance follow-up.

trigger_events.description: Scheduled shift not worked without coverage. Triggers attendance-policy review; HRSD case may be created.

handoffs.description: Confidential garnishment case opened in HRSD; sensitive PII routing required.

trigger_events.description: Court/agency garnishment order received against an employee. PAYROLL must apply withholding; HRSD opens confidential case.

handoffs.description: Case taxonomy updates re-categorize the HR knowledge base so deflection and agent-assist suggestions stay aligned with the routing model.

trigger_events.description: HR-case taxonomy category updated. HRSD routing, knowledge-base mapping, and reporting roll-ups need realignment.

handoffs.description: Case resolution feeds the HR-knowledge improvement loop. Resolution notes and root-cause tags drive article authoring and refinement.

trigger_events.description: HR case is resolved and closed by the HR agent. Downstream consumers (knowledge authoring, learning analytics, audit) react to the closure signal.

handoffs.description: Portal intake submission progresses into the case-management workflow. In-process state transition, same vendor stack, no message moves.

trigger_events.description: Employee submits an HR request via the self-service portal. Case-mgmt picks it up, applies AI triage, and starts the case lifecycle.

handoffs.description: Policy update (leave, harassment) → HRSD exception handling; no standardized machine-readable payload.

trigger_events.description: Policy version incremented and approved; triggers re-attestation.

handoffs.description: Onboarding flags physical-workplace tasks: badge issuance, desk allocation, parking, building access, ergonomic kit. IWMS systems are rarely event-driven; in practice the handoff is a ticket or an email to Facilities. High friction is the norm.

trigger_events.description: Fired when a Onboarding Task is workplace setup required. Publisher domain owns the state transition; subscribers may react by creating downstream artifacts.

handoffs.description: Floor plan changes propagate to workplace space-booking.

trigger_events.description: Floor plan dimensions or layout revised.

handoffs.description: No-show releases feed back into utilization analytics; intra-IWMS lifecycle progression.

trigger_events.description: Fired when a room reservation is auto-released after the grace window. Subscribers (IWMS-SPACE-ANALYTICS) recapture the time slot for utilization reporting.

handoffs.description: Check-in confirms occupancy; intra-IWMS lifecycle progression into utilization analytics.

trigger_events.description: Fired when a desk booking is checked in. Subscribers update occupancy signals (IWMS-SPACE-ANALYTICS) and badge / access systems (IGA) where physical-access provisioning is wired up.

handoffs.description: An editorial step routed to legal review opens a legal-intake record so LSD can track turnaround and decisions.

trigger_events.description: A content entry moves into a review state requiring a specific role (legal, brand, SEO). WSC routes the review task; LSD picks up if legal review.

handoffs.description: Placing a document under legal hold creates / updates the hold record in LSD and freezes retention disposition.

trigger_events.description: An ECM-managed document is placed under legal hold. Retention disposition is suspended; LSD tracks the hold; DLP enforces no-export.

handoffs.description: Eviction initiation triggers a legal matter (filing, notice service, court date tracking); typical legal workflow runs in a separate matter-management system.
handoffs.notes: Multi-shape: cross-vendor-stack (PM + legal-matter system) + alert-without-feedback (eviction status updates rarely flow back to PM). Plus jurisdiction-specific timing complexity.

trigger_events.description: Tenant eviction proceedings have completed; triggers asset-recovery, deposit-disposition, and legal-matter closure.

handoffs.description: Closed-won opportunity triggers contract drafting in CLM. Friction comes from quote-to-contract data mapping and legal redline cycles.

trigger_events.description: Fired when a Opportunity is closed won. Publisher domain owns the state transition; subscribers may react by creating downstream artifacts.

handoffs.description: Signature envelope completion in negotiation hands the executed envelope to the repository for persistence. Intra-domain lifecycle progression; the signed document gets indexed and the linked legal_contract transitions out_for_signature -> signed.

trigger_events.description: All signers on a contract envelope have signed. CLM persists the executed contract; SUB-MGMT provisions the subscription; CRM marks the opportunity won.

handoffs.description: CLM updates contract-performance attributes when a milestone is met, supporting renewal valuation and SLA reporting.
handoffs.notes: target NULL until CLM declares consumer DMDO on `project_billing_milestones`

trigger_events.description: A contractual project milestone has been delivered and signed off, making the milestone billable. ERP-FIN must raise the invoice; CLM updates contract performance; revenue recognition records the trigger.

handoffs.description: Signed engagement letter is the contract artifact; corporate clients may pull it into their CLM for vendor-contract tracking. Most law firms don't push proactively; client requests on demand.
handoffs.notes: Cross-vendor stack; manual handoff is the norm.

trigger_events.description: Client has e-signed the engagement letter; triggers retainer-payment collection, matter creation, and work commencement.
Legal contract executed and active; anchor for renewal countdown and obligation extraction.

handoffs.description: SMP's renewal-watch surfaces a 30-day expiry warning to CLM so the contract document workflow (amendment, renegotiation) can start in time.

trigger_events.description: Fired when a Contract is 30 day warning. Publisher domain owns the state transition; subscribers may react by creating downstream artifacts.

handoffs.description: Approved discount terms must flow into the contract draft in CLM with the correct pricing, term length, and any concession clauses.

trigger_events.description: A discount above the rep's threshold has been approved by sales-ops or finance. Triggers contract drafting in CLM with discount terms; CRM and SALES-PERF reflect approved amount.
Fired when a Contract is signed. Publisher domain owns the state transition; subscribers may react by creating downstream artifacts.
Legal contract approved by counsel; advances to NEGOTIATION->REPOSITORY handoff.

handoffs.description: Clause flagged during negotiation (counterparty pushed back, non-standard language detected, missing protection) is routed back to the authoring/library team for review. Library team decides whether the flag warrants a new approved variant or a clarification on the existing clause.

trigger_events.description: A contract clause has been flagged during review (non-standard, high-risk, requires legal review). CLM routes to the appropriate reviewer.

handoffs.description: CPQ-generated contract draft handed off to CLM for clause assembly and signature routing. Friction when CPQ's term language doesn't match approved CLM templates.

trigger_events.description: CPQ has generated a contract draft from an accepted quote. CLM picks up for clause assembly, redlines, and signature routing.

handoffs.description: Award triggers contract drafting in CLM with the chosen supplier.

trigger_events.description: A sourcing event has been awarded to one or more suppliers. CLM drafts contract; S2P prepares PO; SUP-LIFE updates supplier tier.

handoffs.description: Completed e-signature envelopes flow into CLM as authoritative signature_records. Failure modes: identity-of-signer verification gaps; multi-party-signing edge cases.
handoffs.notes: Cross-platform pattern: the ESIGN vendor integrates with CLM via webhook or batch sync. envelopes is ESIGN-side, signature_records is CLM-side; this handoff carries the envelope and CLM constructs the matching signature_record.

trigger_events.description: An e-signature envelope has been fully signed by all required parties. Downstream: CLM persists the signed contract via signature_records; HR persists offer letters; sales-ops triggers commission and quota effects.

handoffs.description: Executed commercial lease document flows into CLM repository for clause-level search, obligation tracking (TI completion, free-rent expiry), and renewal-window alerts.
handoffs.notes: Bridge between CRE-ops (rent roll) and CLM (document obligations); commonly disconnected in practice.

trigger_events.description: Commercial lease has been signed by both parties; triggers rent-roll update, NOI recalculation, and CAM-allocation update.
Fired when a Contract is renewed. Publisher domain owns the state transition; subscribers may react by creating downstream artifacts.
Legal contract submitted for legal/counsel review; advances from AUTHORING to NEGOTIATION.

handoffs.description: Client-approved estimate must be converted into a signed SOW in CLM before delivery can start. Includes line-item scope, billing terms, deliverable schedule, and approval routing.
handoffs.notes: Friction shape: alert/escalation without feedback loop — estimate approval doesn't auto-create the SOW; CLM-side delays block delivery start.

trigger_events.description: Client signs off on an agency estimate; agency converts it into a binding SOW in CLM and a kicked-off job.

handoffs.description: Accepted quote hands off to CLM for contract authoring — pulls in clause language, populates the agreed terms, routes for signature.

trigger_events.description: Fired when a Contract is accepted. Publisher domain owns the state transition; subscribers may react by creating downstream artifacts.

handoffs.description: Outside counsel engagement letter flows to Contract Lifecycle Management as a managed contract.

trigger_events.description: An outside counsel engagement has been created. Triggers spend tracking and engagement-letter generation.

handoffs.description: Signed engagement letters are the contract artifact; mid-to-large firms increasingly track them in CLM for portfolio visibility and renewal management.
handoffs.notes: Cross-vendor handoff between practice-mgmt and CLM; engagement-letter-platform signing flows are bridging this.

trigger_events.description: Client has e-signed the engagement letter; triggers retainer-payment collection, matter creation, and work commencement.

handoffs.description: Sourcing decision in S2P hands off to CLM to author the contract. Friction sits in clause selection, redline coordination with the counterparty, and the legal-review loop with LSD.

trigger_events.description: Fired when a Contract is contract drafted. Publisher domain owns the state transition; subscribers may react by creating downstream artifacts.

handoffs.description: S2P aligns sourcing and approver thresholds with current policies.

trigger_events.description: A spend policy (per-diem caps, category restrictions, approver thresholds) was updated. EXPENSE, AP-AUTO, S2P, and SPEND-MGMT must refresh rule engines.

handoffs.description: Expired qualifications block new POs until re-qualification.

trigger_events.description: A qualification certification (insurance, ISO, security) has expired. S2P blocks new POs; SUP-LIFE triggers re-qualification.

handoffs.description: ECO release notifies S2P of part-spec changes that affect open requisitions / purchase orders. Sourcing may need to re-RFQ if the supplier cannot meet the new spec; medium friction because the change rarely invalidates the existing PO but routinely requires a side conversation.

trigger_events.description: An ECO has been CAB-approved and released; affected parts now carry new released revisions and the change effective date has passed.

handoffs.description: Qualified suppliers become eligible for sourcing events.

trigger_events.description: A supplier has been fully qualified for procurement. S2P unblocks sourcing; AP-AUTO enables payment; ERP-FIN finalizes vendor master.

handoffs.description: Match exceptions feed back to procurement for PO correction or rebilling.

trigger_events.description: Three-way match failed (price, quantity, or receipt variance). AP-controller intervenes; S2P or SUP-LIFE may need to renegotiate or correct receipt.

handoffs.description: Over-consumption triggers true-up purchase requisitions in S2P.

trigger_events.description: SAM detected license consumption exceeding entitled count. Triggers true-up purchase via S2P or reclamation workflow.

handoffs.description: When SaaS usage forecasts predict seat-count overrun before renewal, SMP triggers a mid-term expansion requisition in S2P to add seats proactively (avoiding emergency procurement at over-pricing).

trigger_events.description: Fired when a Purchase Requisition is exceeded. Publisher domain owns the state transition; subscribers may react by creating downstream artifacts.

handoffs.description: Shadow-IT app that passes the threshold for sanctioning (recurring use, multiple users, business-critical) triggers a procurement requisition in S2P to formalize the relationship.

trigger_events.description: Fired when a Purchase Requisition is requires sanctioning. Publisher domain owns the state transition; subscribers may react by creating downstream artifacts.

handoffs.description: Signed contract in CLM triggers PO creation in S2P. Low friction when the CLM and S2P stack are integrated under a single suite, higher when separate.

trigger_events.description: Fired when a Contract is signed. Publisher domain owns the state transition; subscribers may react by creating downstream artifacts.

handoffs.description: INV-MGMT publishes a replenishment signal; S2P is expected to raise a purchase requisition (or auto-PO if configured). Failure mode: alert without ack, no retry policy.
handoffs.notes: Shape: alert-without-feedback-loop. INV publishes the alert; no confirmation that the PO was raised. Manual follow-up when missed.

trigger_events.description: Stock-on-hand for an item-location pair has fallen below its configured reorder point. Triggers replenishment suggestion against the preferred supplier (or transfer suggestion against a sister warehouse).

handoffs.description: Cloud-provider spend has exceeded a configured threshold (per-account, per-service, monthly). Procurement needs to engage for commitment-discount conversations; finance leadership needs visibility for forecast adjustment.
handoffs.notes: Probabilistic-to-deterministic pattern: spike detection is heuristic, action is binding (commit dollars).

trigger_events.description: Cloud-provider spend exceeded a configured threshold (monthly, daily, per-account, per-service). Cost-center owners and procurement need a heads-up before the spike compounds.

handoffs.description: Project staff-augmentation demand triggers a contingent-worker requisition routed through S2P / VMS.
handoffs.notes: target NULL until S2P declares consumer DMDO on `purchase_requisitions`

trigger_events.description: Fired when a Project is staffing required. Publisher domain owns the state transition; subscribers may react by creating downstream artifacts.

handoffs.description: Expired contracts trigger procurement renewal-decision workflow. Failure modes: auto-renewal clauses missed; silent expiry of long-tail contracts.
handoffs.notes: Calendar-driven; common late-binding issue.

trigger_events.description: A contract has reached its end date without renewal. Procurement and business owners need to decide renewal, replacement, or wind-down.

handoffs.description: Supplier onboarding completion makes the supplier eligible for sourcing events and purchase orders.

trigger_events.description: Fired when a Supplier is approved. Publisher domain owns the state transition; subscribers may react by creating downstream artifacts.

handoffs.description: Low spare-parts levels trigger S2P replenishment requisitions.

trigger_events.description: HAM spare parts on hand for a model fell below the configured threshold. Procurement triggers replenishment via S2P.

handoffs.description: Approved contingent_timesheets × rate_cards produce contingent_invoices that flow into S2P / AP-AUTO for three-way match and payment to the staffing supplier.

trigger_events.description: Fired when a Work Order is invoiced. Publisher domain owns the state transition; subscribers may react by creating downstream artifacts.

handoffs.description: Expiring HAM warranties cue procurement extension renewals.

trigger_events.description: A HAM warranty is approaching expiry (e.g. 90 days). Procurement evaluates extension; ITAM updates support coverage.

handoffs.description: Drug-consumption events trigger reorder thresholds against the veterinary-distributor channel; automated reorder is the norm for chain clinics.
handoffs.notes: Same-vendor PIMS-plus-distributor stacks make this low-friction; cross-distributor still mostly manual.

trigger_events.description: Controlled substance has been dispensed; triggers ledger decrement, perpetual-inventory check, and DEA-compliant audit trail.

handoffs.description: Activated staffing suppliers reconcile with the supplier master.

trigger_events.description: A contingent-labor staffing supplier has been activated in VMS. SUP-LIFE finalizes onboarding; AP-AUTO opens payment channel.

handoffs.description: Quantity variances feed supplier scorecards.

trigger_events.description: Goods receipt quantity differs materially from PO. SUP-LIFE flags supplier; AP-AUTO holds match; S2P investigates.

handoffs.description: Exceptions update supplier scorecard signals.

trigger_events.description: Three-way match failed (price, quantity, or receipt variance). AP-controller intervenes; S2P or SUP-LIFE may need to renegotiate or correct receipt.

handoffs.description: Golden-record changes flow to SUP-LIFE for risk reassessment; approval workflows add latency.

trigger_events.description: Supplier golden record updated; published to S2P, SUP-LIFE.

handoffs.description: Supplier-certification expiry blocks new PO issuance until cert renewed; gates supplier from continued procurement.
handoffs.notes: Fan-out arm of `supplier_certification.expired` — SUP-LIFE side handles supplier-status gating.

trigger_events.description: A supplier certification has passed its expiry date with no renewal received; downstream fans out to FSQM supplier-risk elevation AND SUP-LIFE supplier-onboarding-gate (blocks new POs until renewed).

handoffs.description: Award updates supplier-tier and engagement records.

trigger_events.description: A sourcing event has been awarded to one or more suppliers. CLM drafts contract; S2P prepares PO; SUP-LIFE updates supplier tier.

handoffs.description: Updated ESG score → SUP-LIFE supplier_qualifications field; tier reassessment.

trigger_events.description: ESG score recalculated on refresh.

handoffs.description: Large orgs frequently run SPEND-MGMT (non-PO bill pay) and AP-AUTO (PO-matched three-way-match) in parallel; the same supplier-issued invoice can arrive through either path. Duplicate-invoice detection across two systems with different identifier spaces and routing rules creates ongoing reconciliation burden. Cross-vendor stack pattern with same logical entity.

trigger_events.description: Fired when a Invoice is received. Publisher domain owns the state transition; subscribers may react by creating downstream artifacts.

handoffs.description: Expense reimbursement via AP rather than payroll: the approved expense_report becomes a supplier_invoice paid in the next payment_run.

trigger_events.description: Fired when a Expense Report is approved. Publisher domain owns the state transition; subscribers may react by creating downstream artifacts.

handoffs.description: Bank statements feed AP reconciliation of cleared payments.

trigger_events.description: A bank statement file/feed has arrived. ERP-FIN starts reconciliation; cash_transactions are imported and matched.

handoffs.description: Low-confidence invoice extraction routed to AP clerk for manual review.

trigger_events.description: Extracted record flagged for human review; validator queue receives item.

handoffs.description: Invoice extraction completes; AP-AUTO picks up structured fields for three-way match.

trigger_events.description: Document extraction complete and validated; downstream record creation in AP-AUTO/ECM.

handoffs.description: Expired qualifications hold supplier payments pending re-qualification.

trigger_events.description: A qualification certification (insurance, ISO, security) has expired. S2P blocks new POs; SUP-LIFE triggers re-qualification.

handoffs.description: Annual CAM reconciliation produces tenant true-up invoices (or refunds) that must post to AR; downstream cash collection cycle.
handoffs.notes: Period/cycle-close coupling + cross-vendor stack (CRE platform reconciles, ERP-FIN bills). Tenant disputes drive frequent retro-adjustments.

trigger_events.description: Annual CAM reconciliation has been completed; triggers tenant true-up billing or refund and audit-trail finalization.

handoffs.description: Supplier bank-account changes carry significant fraud risk; identity-reconciliation pattern. Strong vendor-master controls and out-of-band verification gate the propagation to AP-AUTO.

trigger_events.description: Fired when a Supplier is bank changed. Publisher domain owns the state transition; subscribers may react by creating downstream artifacts.

handoffs.description: AP-AUTO unblocks payments once qualification is complete.

trigger_events.description: A supplier has been fully qualified for procurement. S2P unblocks sourcing; AP-AUTO enables payment; ERP-FIN finalizes vendor master.

handoffs.description: Contract amendments propagate to AP-AUTO: updated payment terms, discount schedule, GL coding. Failure modes: retroactive amendments require recalculating already-paid invoices.
handoffs.notes: Period-coupling shape: amendments often have effective dates in past periods.

trigger_events.description: A contract amendment has been executed (price change, scope change, term extension). Finance needs to update payment terms, GL coding, and accruals.

handoffs.description: Approved payment authorizations release invoices into the next payment run.

trigger_events.description: A vendor payment has been authorized within SPEND-MGMT. AP-AUTO releases for payment-run inclusion; ERP-FIN reserves cash.

handoffs.description: Issued POs prime the AP queue for incoming supplier invoices.

trigger_events.description: A PO has been formally issued to a supplier. AP-AUTO awaits invoice; SUP-LIFE tracks supplier activity; ERP-FIN encumbers budget.

handoffs.description: Tax-return filing triggers invoice issuance and posting to firm AR; finance-side accounting cycle.

trigger_events.description: Tax return has been filed (e-filed or paper). Triggers client notification, invoice issuance, working-paper archival, and IRS-acceptance polling.

handoffs.description: AP-AUTO routes payment runs to newly-registered bank accounts.

trigger_events.description: A new corporate bank account has been registered. AP-AUTO routes payment runs; AUDIT and GRC log the new payment surface.

handoffs.description: Contingent invoices enter the AP three-way match queue.

handoffs.description: Approved reimbursable expenses enter the payables queue.

handoffs.notes: Period/cycle-close coupling — monthly close depends on rent-collection batch arriving on time.

handoffs.description: PO amendments require AP to re-price pending matches.

handoffs.description: Goods receipt enables three-way match in AP-AUTO.

handoffs.description: Completed external work orders (3rd-party shops) generate parts/labor invoices that flow into AP for matching and payment.
handoffs.notes: Vendor-invoice matching against work-order line items is the common reconciliation step.

trigger_events.description: Vehicle work order has been completed. Triggers invoice creation, parts-consumption update, vehicle return-to-service, and warranty-claim eligibility check.

handoffs.description: Approaching MSP contract renewal alerts CSM for client engagement.

trigger_events.description: MSP contract is within renewal window. CSM engages for renewal; CRM tracks the expansion opportunity.

handoffs.description: Manual overrides usually correlate with exception cases; CSM gets context to handle customer questions and slipped ETAs.

trigger_events.description: A human operator or downstream WMS overrode the computed sourcing plan. CSM and B2C-COMM may need to refresh promised dates; analytics records the override reason.

handoffs.description: Closed-won opportunity in CRM triggers entitlement provisioning in CSM ahead of (or in parallel to) subscription activation in SUB-MGMT. Important for fast onboarding of high-touch customers.

trigger_events.description: Fired when a Opportunity is closed won. Publisher domain owns the state transition; subscribers may react by creating downstream artifacts.

handoffs.description: Subscription activation creates the matching customer_entitlements record in CSM: tier mapped to support level, named contacts seeded, SLA targets bound. Friction sits in mapping subscription plan SKUs to support tiers, which is rarely 1:1.

trigger_events.description: Fired when a Customer Subscription is activated. Publisher domain owns the state transition; subscribers may react by creating downstream artifacts.

handoffs.description: Inbound social message (comment, DM, mention-reply) classified as a service issue (complaint, order question, technical problem) triggers case creation in CSM with the message payload, customer context (if resolvable), and channel metadata. Failure modes: classifier misfires flood the CSM queue with non-service items; social-handle-to-customer-record reconciliation is unreliable across networks; cases reopened in CSM rarely sync back to the originating SMM thread, fragmenting conversation history.
handoffs.notes: Probabilistic-signal-becomes-deterministic-action pattern; aggravated by identity reconciliation across handle namespaces.

trigger_events.description: Fired when a Social Message is received. Publisher domain owns the state transition; subscribers may react by creating downstream artifacts.

handoffs.description: Listening pipeline detects a brand/product mention with negative sentiment or high reach off-channel (Reddit thread, Twitter complaint without @mention, review-site post) and routes it to CSM for proactive outreach. Failure modes: sentiment classification false positives consume agent time; off-channel mentions rarely include a resolvable customer identity; coordination with PR/comms is manual.
handoffs.notes: Off-channel companion to social_message.received; same probabilistic-signal shape but without an inbox conversation to reply into.

trigger_events.description: Fired when a Social Mention is detected. Publisher domain owns the state transition; subscribers may react by creating downstream artifacts.

handoffs.description: CSM activates white-glove monitoring and direct comms with beta participants while the program is live.

handoffs.description: Payment failure opens a customer-success case in CSM for proactive intervention — distinct from automated dunning emails, this is the human-touch path for higher-value accounts.

trigger_events.description: Fired when a Customer Case is failed. Publisher domain owns the state transition; subscribers may react by creating downstream artifacts.

handoffs.description: Customer-facing refund payment failures need CSM awareness so the customer can be contacted before they discover the missing refund themselves.

handoffs.description: Subscriptions entering the renewal window (90 days from term-end by default) must surface in CSM for the renewal motion. Failure modes: auto-renew customers slip through CSM's view; multi-product subscriptions have staggered terms.

trigger_events.description: A subscription is within the renewal window (typically 90 days from term end). CSM should engage with the customer for renewal motion.

handoffs.description: Strategic account planning flags declining health; CSM engages for retention. Failure modes: health score components disagree (usage, sentiment, billing) — CSM unclear what to address.

trigger_events.description: An account's composite health score has declined materially. CSM needs to engage for retention; sales for expansion-replan.

handoffs.description: Escalated calls trigger CSM case re-assignment to a specialist or supervisor. Failure modes: original agent's context lost in handoff.

handoffs.description: Real-time negative sentiment triggers CSM triage for outreach. Failure modes: AI sentiment scoring is unreliable; false positives drown the queue.

trigger_events.description: A resource rolls off a project (planned end reached, early release, or scope change). Returns capacity to the HCM bench, closes the WORK-MGMT seat, and may trigger SWP demand-replan.

handoffs.description: A slipped billing milestone surfaces on the project delivery plan so the delivery team can replan or recover.

trigger_events.description: A scheduled billing milestone has not been delivered by its target date. Cash-forecast in EPM/ERP-FIN must reflect the slip and CLM may need to assess contract penalty exposure.

handoffs.description: Committed allocations feed forward-looking cost into project financials ahead of actual time entries.

trigger_events.description: A tentative resource-allocation plan transitions to committed status. HCM treats the named hours as booked capacity; CLM links the allocation to the underlying engagement contract.

handoffs.description: Task completion updates percentage-of-completion inputs that project financials consume for revenue recognition.

trigger_events.description: A delivery task on the project plan has been marked complete. WORK-MGMT mirrors the status; PSA aggregates for milestone progress and EPM consumes for delivery KPI rollup.

handoffs.description: Approved time becomes billable inventory for invoice generation in project financials.

trigger_events.description: Fired when a Time Entry is approved. Publisher domain owns the state transition; subscribers may react by creating downstream artifacts.

handoffs.description: Approved expenses become billable / pass-through inventory for invoice generation in project financials.

trigger_events.description: Fired when a Expense Report is approved. Publisher domain owns the state transition; subscribers may react by creating downstream artifacts.

handoffs.description: Milestone completion in delivery triggers invoice creation in project financials.

trigger_events.description: A contractual project milestone has been delivered and signed off, making the milestone billable. ERP-FIN must raise the invoice; CLM updates contract performance; revenue recognition records the trigger.

handoffs.description: Project-tagged time_entries feed PSA for utilization and billable-hours calculation.

trigger_events.description: Fired when a Time Entry is approved. Publisher domain owns the state transition; subscribers may react by creating downstream artifacts.
Fired when a Lead is qualified. Publisher domain owns the state transition; subscribers may react by creating downstream artifacts.

handoffs.notes: Intra-CRM lifecycle progression: closed-won opportunity transitions the account (customers) to active-customer state and primes expansion-ready signals in CRM-ACCT-MGT.

trigger_events.description: Fired when a Opportunity is closed won. Publisher domain owns the state transition; subscribers may react by creating downstream artifacts.

handoffs.notes: Intra-CRM lifecycle progression: lead conversion materializes the account (customers) record in CRM-ACCT-MGT.

trigger_events.description: A CRM lead has been converted into a customer (account), contact, and optionally an opportunity. Suppresses ongoing nurture in MA, primes onboarding-readiness signals, and feeds funnel-conversion analytics in revenue intelligence.

handoffs.notes: Intra-CRM lifecycle progression: lead conversion materializes the contact (crm_contacts) record in CRM-ACCT-MGT.

trigger_events.description: A CRM lead has been converted into a customer (account), contact, and optionally an opportunity. Suppresses ongoing nurture in MA, primes onboarding-readiness signals, and feeds funnel-conversion analytics in revenue intelligence.

handoffs.notes: Intra-CRM lifecycle progression: optional opportunity is created at lead-conversion time when the lead carries a deal signal.

trigger_events.description: A CRM lead has been converted into a customer (account), contact, and optionally an opportunity. Suppresses ongoing nurture in MA, primes onboarding-readiness signals, and feeds funnel-conversion analytics in revenue intelligence.

handoffs.description: CRM updates the customer's lifetime-value and returns-rate signals; high return rates may downgrade segmentation.

trigger_events.description: Returned merchandise has been received and inspected at the return location. Triggers refund release in ERP-FIN, restock or disposition decision, and CSM case close.
Fired when a Opportunity is stage changed. Publisher domain owns the state transition; subscribers may react by creating downstream artifacts.

handoffs.description: Social engagement enriches CRM contact records. Friction in identity-resolution across handles.

trigger_events.description: Fired when a Customer is recorded. Publisher domain owns the state transition; subscribers may react by creating downstream artifacts.

handoffs.description: On booking completion, the customer and trip history are pushed to CRM so the operator builds a guest relationship beyond the single booking.

trigger_events.description: A booking is completed after the activity takes place. Feeds the customer record and history downstream and prompts a review request.

handoffs.description: Completed nurture without conversion returns the lead to CRM for re-routing or recycle.

trigger_events.description: A lead has completed all steps of a nurture journey without converting. CRM may downgrade or recycle; MA may enroll in a longer-cadence sequence.

handoffs.description: Each weekly delivery is a customer-engagement touchpoint; missed pickups, swap-rate trends, and pause-week behavior are churn-risk signals fed back to CRM.
handoffs.notes: Probabilistic-signal pattern — engagement scoring is heuristic; vendor maturity in this loop is uneven across the FDS market.

trigger_events.description: A weekly CSA share has been delivered or picked up; downstream is a customer-engagement touch-point and a churn-risk feedback signal.
Fired when a Opportunity is requires quote. Publisher domain owns the state transition; subscribers may react by creating downstream artifacts.

handoffs.description: CRM updates opportunity amount and stage with the discounted value so forecast and quota tracking are accurate.

trigger_events.description: A discount has been applied to a quote line or quote header. CRM updates opportunity amounts; ERP-FIN models margin impact; SALES-PERF tracks discounting behavior.

handoffs.description: Cadence reply pauses outreach and creates a CRM activity. Native CRM connectors on all major SALES-ENG platforms.

trigger_events.description: Recipient replied to a sales email. Strong intent signal; cadence pauses, sales rep notified, CRM activity logged.

handoffs.description: Transcribed call attached to CRM activity. Most conversation-intelligence vendors offer first-class CRM sync.

trigger_events.description: Recording transcription completed. Downstream conversation intelligence and revenue intelligence consume the transcript for insights and risk signals.

handoffs.description: CSM-identified expansion creates a CRM opportunity. Often a manual handoff with poor close-the-loop visibility.

trigger_events.description: CSM has identified an expansion opportunity (more seats, additional modules, tier upgrade). SUB-MGMT prepares the proposal; CRM creates the expansion opportunity.

handoffs.description: Customer case creation logs an activity on the CRM account. Native CSM-CRM integration on shared platforms.

trigger_events.description: Fired when a Customer Event is created. Publisher domain owns the state transition; subscribers may react by creating downstream artifacts.

handoffs.description: Subscription upgrade closes the CRM expansion opportunity and updates account ARR.

trigger_events.description: Customer subscription upgraded (more seats, higher tier, additional modules). SUB-MGMT updates billing; CSM logs expansion; CRM closes expansion opportunity.

handoffs.description: CRM records new customer order in account context; revenue metrics + CSM visibility.

trigger_events.description: Order created from checkout; cart → order_lines conversion complete.

handoffs.description: Quote acceptance advances the linked opportunity to closed-won pending signature.

trigger_events.description: Buyer has accepted the quote (typically via e-sign or portal acceptance). CLM creates the contract draft; CRM advances opportunity to closed-won pending signature; SUB-MGMT prepares subscription provisioning.

handoffs.description: CRM entitlements and CPQ catalog need to reflect newly available features so reps can position and quote them.

trigger_events.description: A product feature has shipped to general availability. DXP needs marketing-page updates; CRM updates entitlements; CDP refreshes segment definitions that key on feature usage.

handoffs.description: Qualified buyer/seller leads flow into CRM-cluster contacts and the agent's CRM for nurture and conversion tracking.

trigger_events.description: Real-estate buyer or seller lead has been qualified by the agent; transitions probabilistic intent into a deterministic next-action queue.

handoffs.description: Subscription activation marks the account as an active customer in CRM, updates ARR rollups, and unlocks customer-success workflows. Low friction when same-vendor stack; medium when CRM and billing are separate.

trigger_events.description: Fired when a Customer Subscription is activated. Publisher domain owns the state transition; subscribers may react by creating downstream artifacts.

handoffs.description: Storefront signup creates the canonical customer record in CRM. Low friction in B2C-native integrated stacks; medium in stitched-together stacks.

trigger_events.description: Fired when a Customer is signed up. Publisher domain owns the state transition; subscribers may react by creating downstream artifacts.

handoffs.description: Cluster of critical cases or sustained low CSAT triggers an account-health-drop signal back to CRM, surfacing as a churn-risk flag on the account. High friction because the threshold definition is org-specific and the CRM-side account-health field rarely has good UX for the alert.

trigger_events.description: Fired when a Customer is critical health drop. Publisher domain owns the state transition; subscribers may react by creating downstream artifacts.

handoffs.description: CDP-detected lifecycle stage change (new → engaged → loyal → at-risk → churned) updates the customer record in CRM. Friction comes from CDP's lifecycle model not matching CRM's account-status taxonomy.

trigger_events.description: Fired when a Customer is lifecycle changed. Publisher domain owns the state transition; subscribers may react by creating downstream artifacts.

handoffs.description: Social interaction with explicit intent, DM asking pricing, click-through on a lead-gen form, message-ad reply, converts into a CRM-mastered lead with handle, captured form data, and source attribution. Failure modes: handle-to-existing-contact reconciliation produces duplicate leads; form-data quality from social lead-gen ads is inconsistent across networks.
handoffs.notes: Identity-reconciliation pattern; usually well-supported by MA-to-CRM connectors but quality is uneven.

trigger_events.description: Fired when a Lead is captured. Publisher domain owns the state transition; subscribers may react by creating downstream artifacts.

handoffs.description: Completed calls (and their disposition, duration, recording link) log to the CRM activity timeline. Low friction because activity-sync is a core SALES-ENG ↔ CRM integration that vendors invest in heavily.

trigger_events.description: Fired when a Sales Activity is completed. Publisher domain owns the state transition; subscribers may react by creating downstream artifacts.

handoffs.description: Conversation-intelligence-extracted insight (competitor mentioned, pricing objection, decision-maker identified, commitment made) updates the opportunity record in CRM — fields, custom flags, risk score. Friction comes from rep adoption of the AI-suggested fields, not the integration itself.

trigger_events.description: Fired when a Opportunity is captured. Publisher domain owns the state transition; subscribers may react by creating downstream artifacts.

handoffs.description: Sales reps need the new line in CRM opportunity records and the CPQ catalog; product-master propagation is a recurring integration headache.

trigger_events.description: A new product line is now live. Catalog updates flow to B2C-COMM and CPQ; CRM enables the line on opportunity records; ERP-FIN sets up the revenue stream.

handoffs.description: Nurture journey completion (whether successful conversion or exit) updates lead status in CRM. Low friction in same-vendor all-in-one stacks; medium when MA and CRM are separate.

trigger_events.description: Fired when a Lead is completed. Publisher domain owns the state transition; subscribers may react by creating downstream artifacts.

handoffs.description: Depleted retainer triggers CRM expansion opportunity. Often manual; close-the-loop is weak.

trigger_events.description: Client retainer fully consumed. PSA halts unbilled work; CRM expansion opportunity may be created; ERP-FIN reflects final draw-down.

handoffs.description: 30-day renewal warning surfaces in CRM for account-rep action.

trigger_events.description: Fired when a Contract is 30 day warning. Publisher domain owns the state transition; subscribers may react by creating downstream artifacts.

handoffs.description: Missed meetings flag opportunity stage-back or extra cadence iteration. Failure modes: false no-shows from calendar timezone errors; rep-side reschedules not captured.
handoffs.notes: Engagement-data quality issue.

trigger_events.description: A scheduled sales meeting was missed by the prospect. The opportunity may need a stage-back or extra cadence iteration.

handoffs.description: Completed cadences signal an opportunity stage check. Failure modes: cadence completion without engagement should mark for nurture, not advance.
handoffs.notes: Tight loop: SALES-ENG → CRM are typically same-vendor.

trigger_events.description: A sales engagement cadence has run to completion (all steps executed). The associated opportunity record needs a stage check; if no engagement was achieved, the lead may downgrade or move to nurture.

handoffs.description: Revenue intelligence flags a high-risk opportunity; CRM surfaces it to the rep. Failure modes: too many alerts dilute attention; AI risk scores not explainable.
handoffs.notes: Probabilistic-to-deterministic shape: REV-INTEL inference, CRM intervention.

trigger_events.description: Revenue intelligence has flagged an opportunity as high-risk (slipping close date, lack of activity, sentiment shift). CRM should surface for sales-rep intervention.

handoffs.description: CRM records payment failure in customer case for CS follow-up.

trigger_events.description: Payment method rejected.

handoffs.description: CSA membership activation creates or enriches the underlying CRM-mastered customer record with membership status, share preferences, and pickup location.
handoffs.notes: Cloud-native FDS vendors typically integrate directly with mainstream CRM and email-marketing platforms as the CRM target.

trigger_events.description: A CSA membership has been activated for the current season; downstream creates / enriches the CRM-mastered customer record for ongoing engagement.

handoffs.description: Resolved golden ID + merged attributes; CRM links operational record.

trigger_events.description: New deduplicated customer golden record resolved; published to CRM/CSM/SUB-MGMT/CDP.

handoffs.description: MA-driven scoring crosses the MQL threshold; the lead routes to CRM with a recommended owner. Friction comes from definition drift — what counts as MQL, who owns routing, what happens to disqualified leads — and from the lead-to-contact-to-opportunity conversion chain inside CRM.

trigger_events.description: Fired when a Lead is qualified. Publisher domain owns the state transition; subscribers may react by creating downstream artifacts.

handoffs.description: Dispatched route triggers CRM/CCAAS ETA notifications to subscribers.

trigger_events.description: A delivery route has been dispatched with manifest and driver; downstream CRM notifies customers of ETA and FOOD-TRACE attaches lot/temperature attestations.

handoffs.description: Qualified leads routed to CRM for sales pickup. Tight integration on all major MA platforms.

trigger_events.description: A lead's predictive score has crossed the qualified-handoff threshold. Sales engagement should pick it up for an outreach cadence.

handoffs.description: Tier upgrades surface in CRM for account-tag refresh, VIP treatment, sales-rep awareness. Failure modes: tier change effective dates and CRM record sync lag.
handoffs.notes: Identity reconciliation: LOYALTY member_id and CRM customer_id may differ.

trigger_events.description: A loyalty member has been upgraded to a higher tier (qualifying threshold met). CRM should know for VIP treatment; marketing for celebration messaging.

handoffs.description: Detected intent routes to CRM for opportunity creation or case enrichment. Failure modes: intent disambiguation when multiple intents in one conversation.
handoffs.notes: AI-mediated routing.

trigger_events.description: Conversational AI has identified a customer intent (billing question, technical issue, churn signal, upgrade interest). Downstream routing to CRM / case-management / sales-engagement.

handoffs.description: Declining health score surfaces churn risk to CRM for sales-rep awareness during renewal.

trigger_events.description: A customer's composite health score has declined materially. CSM needs retention motion; SUB-MGMT needs to flag for renewal risk.

handoffs.description: New customer merge rule re-evaluates pending duplicates; CRM golden records may be re-keyed.

trigger_events.description: A new MDM merge rule is published; pending duplicate sets re-evaluated against the rule.

handoffs.description: Mystery shopper findings feed CRM/CSM coaching cases for customer-facing associates.

trigger_events.description: A mystery shopper visit report has been submitted; downstream CRM/CSM may open a coaching case for low-scoring service interactions.

handoffs.description: CRM uses 'requested-features-shipped' as renewal and expansion talk-track on the account record; close-the-loop comms run via CSM and DXP.

trigger_events.description: A feature request has been delivered in a release. Notifies CRM-tracked requesters, fires close-the-loop comms via DXP and CSM, and updates the customer record.

handoffs.description: BOPIS visits are CRM-relevant in-store engagement signals; clienteling apps surface the upcoming visit to store associates.

trigger_events.description: A buy-online-pickup-in-store (BOPIS) order has been created. The destination store is notified for staging; B2C-COMM shows pickup instructions; CRM links the visit to the customer record.

handoffs.description: Updated harvest forecast feeds CRM CSA-subscriber communication about availability changes.

trigger_events.description: A harvest forecast has been updated with revised yield/timing; downstream ERP-FIN updates revenue projection and CRM informs pre-sale subscribers/CSA members.

handoffs.description: Partner-sourced referrals flow into CRM lead-routing. Failure modes: dedup against existing prospects; partner-attribution edge cases.
handoffs.notes: Cross-vendor stack: PRM platform distinct from CRM in most stacks.

trigger_events.description: A partner-sourced referral has been qualified and is ready for the sales engagement motion. CRM lead-routing needs to assign to a partner-aware sales rep.

handoffs.description: Joint opportunities flow from PRM into CRM with split-credit metadata. Failure modes: commission split rules need re-evaluation per deal; partner identity drift.
handoffs.notes: Identity reconciliation: partner_id and account_owner_id are separate identifier spaces.

trigger_events.description: A joint opportunity has been created with a channel partner. Both internal sales and partner-rep need visibility; commissions may need split logic.

handoffs.description: Identified customer intent (upgrade, churn signal, billing issue) routed to CRM for sales/CS follow-up.

trigger_events.description: Conversational AI has identified a customer intent (billing question, technical issue, churn signal, upgrade interest). Downstream routing to CRM / case-management / sales-engagement.

handoffs.description: CCaaS contact creates/updates CRM activity. Friction comes from CTI/CRM screen-pop latency and identity matching.

trigger_events.description: A CCaaS contact (call, chat, email, social) has been recorded. CSM links to the customer case; WFM uses for agent occupancy.

handoffs.description: Engagement completion notifies the account team so success milestones, references, and renewal motions can be triggered.

trigger_events.description: Fired when an engagement is delivery-complete. CRM and account-team systems react; PSA financials closes out residual billing.

handoffs.description: New customer site activated; CRM enriches the account record with the service-address footprint.

trigger_events.description: Site moves from prospect to active service. May trigger CRM account update and contract creation.

handoffs.description: PM overdue on equipment at customer site; CRM account-manager receives escalation signal for proactive outreach.

trigger_events.description: PM cycle past grace window. Escalation alert sent to account manager.

handoffs.description: Downgrades are churn-risk signals: lower tier, fewer seats, removed modules. CRM needs the opportunity record reopened for expansion replan; CSM needs to run retention motion.
handoffs.notes: Going-away pattern: downgrades are harder to catch than upgrades because they arrive via many channels (in-app, support ticket, contractual amendment).

trigger_events.description: A customer subscription has been downgraded (lower tier, fewer seats, removed modules). Churn-risk signal; CRM needs expansion-replan, CSM needs retention motion.
A new opportunity has been created. Feeds pipeline quota tracking in sales performance and forecast inputs in revenue intelligence.

handoffs.description: Expired quotes need rep follow-up to re-engage or re-quote. Failure modes: silent expiry; reps unaware until customer escalates.
handoffs.notes: Calendar-driven low-friction.

trigger_events.description: A CPQ-generated quote has reached its validity expiry without acceptance. Sales rep needs to re-engage or re-quote.
A scheduled sales meeting was missed by the prospect. The opportunity may need a stage-back or extra cadence iteration.

handoffs.description: Completed influencer-marketing campaign performance (reach, engagement, conversions, earned media value, content samples) feeds back from the influencer tool to MA campaign attribution and ROI reporting. Failure modes: cross-vendor schemas don't align on attribution windows; influencer-driven conversions are hard to attribute deterministically; payout reconciliation is often manual.
handoffs.notes: Cross-vendor stack pattern, the influencer module is rarely part of the MA platform; lossy aggregation common.

trigger_events.description: Fired when a Campaign is completed. Publisher domain owns the state transition; subscribers may react by creating downstream artifacts.

handoffs.description: Coupon redemption closes the marketing campaign attribution loop.

trigger_events.description: Coupon redeemed at checkout. ERP-FIN books the discount; LOYALTY may award bonus points; MA tracks campaign ROI.

handoffs.description: Lapsed loyalty members trigger marketing-automation win-back motion. Failure modes: lapse criteria (inactivity threshold) tuning; false lapses for seasonal customers.
handoffs.notes: Marketing automation typically same-vendor with MA platform.

trigger_events.description: A loyalty member's status has lapsed (inactivity threshold, missed renewal, opt-out). Marketing should engage in win-back motion.

handoffs.description: Contact updates in CRM (new contact, status change, opt-in change, account ownership) sync to MA so audience lists and campaigns stay current. Batch-sync is the typical pattern — real-time would be ideal but most stacks accept hourly or daily latency here.

trigger_events.description: Fired when a Contact is synced. Publisher domain owns the state transition; subscribers may react by creating downstream artifacts.

handoffs.description: Drop-out from a critical journey step enrolls the visitor into a recovery cadence in marketing automation.

trigger_events.description: A visitor drops out of a journey step (timeout, exit page). MA enrolls into recovery cadence; CDP updates churn-risk attributes.

handoffs.description: When a marketing plan is approved, its planned campaigns are handed to marketing-execution to be built and sent. Payload: the campaign the plan line funds.

trigger_events.description: A marketing plan has been approved and its plan lines are ready to be funded and scheduled. Consumers: budget allocation, calendar publication.

handoffs.description: Activating a DXP experience publishes audience and lifecycle context that marketing automation uses to align outbound campaigns.

trigger_events.description: A DXP experience (campaign-tied digital surface) goes live. MA and CDP align audience activation; analytics begins capture.

handoffs.description: Conversion outcomes inform marketing automation nurture and suppression: convert-then-suppress, retarget non-converters.

trigger_events.description: A server-side conversion event was matched to paid social delivery. Downstream: attribution and incrementality, revenue analytics.

handoffs.description: Marketing-Automation campaigns reference content snippets, hero copy, and CTAs that live in the CMS, but the link between a CMS entry and a campaign template is rarely event-driven. Marketers manually copy CMS content into the MA email/SMS template; CMS-side changes after the campaign is built don't propagate. Shadow-data pattern: the campaign's content of record diverges silently from the CMS source.

trigger_events.description: Fired when a Content Entry is published. Publisher domain owns the state transition; subscribers may react by creating downstream artifacts.

handoffs.description: MA records checkout-funnel step for analytics + attribution.

trigger_events.description: Customer entered checkout flow; cart locked, shipping quoted.

handoffs.description: CDP-defined segment activates into MA for campaign targeting. Friction sits in segment-definition portability — what CDP calls 'high-value-active' may not map cleanly to MA's list-and-criteria model, requiring sync logic.

trigger_events.description: Fired when a Audience Segment is activated. Publisher domain owns the state transition; subscribers may react by creating downstream artifacts.

handoffs.description: MA receives abandoned-cart triggers for segmented email nurture. Payload: product list, total value, customer contact.

trigger_events.description: Cart inactivity timeout or explicit session close without conversion; triggers MA nurture.

handoffs.description: Published social post tied to a multi-channel campaign in MA emits a publish event with channel, post URL, and tracked UTM parameters so MA can attribute downstream conversions to the campaign. Failure modes: campaign-id mapping between SMM tool and MA platform is brittle; UTM consistency depends on author discipline; engagement data from the social network arrives on a different cadence than the publish event.
handoffs.notes: Cross-vendor stack pattern; weakest of the six handoffs — implementation-dependent and bypassable in single-vendor stacks.

trigger_events.description: Fired when a Social Post is published. Publisher domain owns the state transition; subscribers may react by creating downstream artifacts.

handoffs.description: Journey stage transitions drive personalized commerce experience (recommendations, banners, offers).

trigger_events.description: Customer entered a new journey stage (awareness → consideration → purchase → retention → advocacy). MA triggers stage-appropriate campaign; CSM may step up engagement for at-risk stages.

handoffs.description: Refreshed attributes drive personalized commerce experiences (banners, recommendations, dynamic pricing).

trigger_events.description: Computed customer attributes (LTV, churn-propensity, segment membership) have been recomputed. MA refreshes nurture eligibility; CSM updates health-score inputs; LOYALTY revisits tier eligibility.

handoffs.description: Discontinued SKU must be pulled from storefront and marketplace listings. Multi-shape high-friction: leaver pattern (going-away signal often arrives via different channel than original arrival) + cross-vendor stack.
handoffs.notes: target NULL until B2C-COMM is modularized. Leaver-pattern handoff.

trigger_events.description: Product is no longer offered; downstream systems must stop fulfillment for net-new orders.

handoffs.description: Storefront and order-status pages reflect the allocated node and refined ETA to the customer.

trigger_events.description: An order line has been allocated to a specific inventory location. Triggers WMS pick-pack, ERP-FIN inventory reservation accounting, and B2C-COMM order-status update.

handoffs.description: New SKU sync to storefront-facing catalog; B2C-COMM creates or updates the `commerce_products` record.

trigger_events.description: New SKU has been authored in the inventory catalog. Syncs to storefront-facing PIM-like catalogs (B2C-COMM) for product publication.

handoffs.description: Storefront must suppress that node from availability and ETA computations when capacity is exhausted, otherwise it will keep promising orders the node cannot fulfill.

trigger_events.description: On-hand units at a location crossed the configured capacity or safety-stock threshold. Sourcing and replenishment workflows should rebalance; B2C-COMM may suppress availability promises from that node.

handoffs.description: Storefront refreshes product copy, banner content, or marketing pages when CMS publishes. Common in composable-commerce stacks pairing a headless commerce engine with a headless CMS. Failure modes: stale storefront caches when the webhook silently fails; mis-localized content when the storefront's locale resolution diverges from the CMS's.

trigger_events.description: Fired when a Content Entry is published. Publisher domain owns the state transition; subscribers may react by creating downstream artifacts.

handoffs.description: Reward redemption fulfilled via B2C commerce when reward is a physical product or storefront credit.

trigger_events.description: A member has redeemed points for a reward. CRM logs the engagement; B2C-COMM may fulfill physical reward; ERP-FIN books the redemption liability movement.

handoffs.description: Coordinated go-live of a content release and commerce changes (new collection launch, pricing campaign). The release event fans out to the storefront which invalidates caches and refreshes catalog-adjacent content. Friction increases when the commerce platform's content cache TTL is uncoordinated with the release window.

trigger_events.description: Fired when a Content Release is published. Publisher domain owns the state transition; subscribers may react by creating downstream artifacts.

handoffs.description: Segment activation drives personalized storefront experience: which products surface, which banners show, what discount tier applies. Friction is medium — real-time segment evaluation at storefront render-time is non-trivial latency-wise.

trigger_events.description: Fired when a Audience Segment is activated. Publisher domain owns the state transition; subscribers may react by creating downstream artifacts.

handoffs.description: PIM publishes a product release; B2C-COMM refreshes its storefront-runtime cache (commerce_products). Failure modes: cross-vendor cache invalidation (PIM and commerce often different vendors), partial-publish where some attributes propagate before others, CDN URL mismatch between PIM-managed assets and storefront media library.
handoffs.notes: target NULL until B2C-COMM is modularized. Multi-shape: cross-vendor stack + alert-without-feedback-loop (rejected publishes routinely need manual remediation in PIM).

trigger_events.description: Product is now live on one or more syndication channels; storefronts, inventory, and CPQ become eligible to read.

handoffs.description: Storefront sends the ready-for-pickup notification (push, email, SMS) to the customer with location and hours.

trigger_events.description: BOPIS order is staged and ready for customer pickup. Notification is sent via B2C-COMM; CSM monitors for SLA breach.

handoffs.description: Storefront calls OMS sourcing in-line during checkout (or asynchronously post-checkout) to display promised-delivery dates and shipping options.

trigger_events.description: The OMS sourcing engine has produced a sourcing decision for an order (chosen node, split lines, carrier). Feeds B2C-COMM promised-delivery dates and ERP-FIN cost-of-fulfillment planning.

handoffs.description: Promised-delivery dates and source-node displayed to the shopper must be refreshed when allocations move; stale ETAs erode trust.

trigger_events.description: An existing allocation has been moved to a different inventory location (capacity issue, faster ship, store-cancellation). Downstream pick instructions and ETA updates flow to B2C-COMM and CSM.

handoffs.description: Personalization rules referencing commerce SKUs/categories are pushed to the storefront merchandising engine for consistent experiences across page and product detail.

trigger_events.description: A personalization rule is enabled in production. CDP segment dependencies are resolved and rule evaluation engines reload.

handoffs.description: Issued invoice surfaces in the customer portal.

trigger_events.description: A customer invoice has been issued. ERP-FIN records receivable; B2C-COMM/CSM customer portal surfaces the invoice; dunning timer starts.

handoffs.description: Social engagement events (likes, shares, comments, video-view depth, story interactions, profile visits) stream to CDP to enrich the unified customer profile with behavioral signals across channels. Failure modes: identity reconciliation across per-network handle namespaces is unreliable; many engagement events lack a resolvable user; cross-platform deduplication of the same person is hard.
handoffs.notes: Identity-reconciliation pattern at scale; the single biggest CDP-enrichment headache in the social stack.

trigger_events.description: Fired when a Customer is recorded. Publisher domain owns the state transition; subscribers may react by creating downstream artifacts.

handoffs.description: Form submission populates CDP identity-graph and behavior profile.

trigger_events.description: Web form (gated content, demo request, contact-us) has been submitted. MA captures lead; CDP merges to identity graph; CRM lead-routing kicks in.

handoffs.description: Newly published DXP segments are mirrored to the CDP so identity and journey orchestration can reuse the same definitions.

trigger_events.description: A DXP audience segment definition is published. CDP, MA, and B2C-COMM consume the segment for personalization and targeting.

handoffs.description: CDP creates and maintains the beta cohort segment for tailored messaging, in-product cues, and analytics.

trigger_events.description: A beta program has been opened to enrolled participants. CRM tags participating accounts; CSM activates white-glove monitoring; CDP segments the cohort for tailored comms.

handoffs.description: Golden record changes must propagate within SLA; identity corrections time-sensitive for marketing.

trigger_events.description: Customer golden record updated; published to all consumers.

handoffs.description: Golden record updates propagate to CDP identity graph.

trigger_events.description: Source record merged into a golden record; downstream consumers receive updated golden.

handoffs.description: Product catalog updates feed CDP for personalization and segmentation.

trigger_events.description: A new product has been published in the commerce catalog. CDP can include in segments; MA can launch awareness campaign; B2C storefront surfaces it.

handoffs.description: Visitor journey-step entries stream into the CDP identity graph, updating lifecycle stage and feeding propensity models.

trigger_events.description: A visitor crosses into a defined journey step. MA triggers cadence; CDP updates lifecycle stage; B2C-COMM applies merchandising rule.

handoffs.description: Case lifecycle events (created, escalated, resolved, CSAT received) flow from CSM to CDP so the unified profile reflects support interactions. Friction is medium — case identifiers need to resolve to the CDP profile, and case context (severity, root cause) needs schema mapping.

trigger_events.description: Fired when a Customer Event is created. Publisher domain owns the state transition; subscribers may react by creating downstream artifacts.

handoffs.description: Opportunity-stage transitions and sales-activity events flow from CRM to CDP. Friction sits in the identity match — CRM contacts must reconcile to CDP-resolved customer profiles, which is not always 1:1.

trigger_events.description: Fired when a Opportunity is stage changed. Publisher domain owns the state transition; subscribers may react by creating downstream artifacts.

handoffs.description: Storefront events (page view, product view, add-to-cart, checkout, return, search) flow from commerce to CDP for behavioral profile enrichment and segment recomputation.

trigger_events.description: Fired when a Customer Event is interaction. Publisher domain owns the state transition; subscribers may react by creating downstream artifacts.

handoffs.description: Campaign delivery, open, click, bounce, and unsubscribe events flow from MA to CDP for unified event-stream aggregation. Low friction because event-stream ingestion is exactly what CDP tools are built for.

trigger_events.description: Fired when a Campaign is event recorded. Publisher domain owns the state transition; subscribers may react by creating downstream artifacts.

handoffs.description: CDP refreshes feature-affinity segments used downstream by marketing, CSM playbooks, and pricing experiments.

trigger_events.description: A feature's active-user adoption crossed the configured target (or fell below floor). CSM uses for expansion or churn-risk conversation; CDP refreshes feature-affinity segments.

handoffs.description: Marketing engagement events (email open, click, content view, form submission) feed CDP for profile enrichment and segment recomputation.

trigger_events.description: Fired when a Campaign is engagement recorded. Publisher domain owns the state transition; subscribers may react by creating downstream artifacts.

handoffs.description: CPQ pulls the attribute schema and option dependencies for a newly-published product so the configurator UI can offer it. Medium friction: attribute-shape changes break existing CPQ rules.
handoffs.notes: target NULL until CPQ is modularized.

trigger_events.description: Product is now live on one or more syndication channels; storefronts, inventory, and CPQ become eligible to read.

handoffs.description: Account tier change cascades to CPQ for price-list assignment.

trigger_events.description: An account's tier classification (strategic / enterprise / mid-market / SMB) has changed. Triggers territory or quota realignment in sales performance and CSM re-segmentation.

handoffs.description: Opportunity reaches the proposal stage; CPQ generates a configured quote (product mix, discount structure, term). Friction sits in product-catalog sync between CRM and CPQ and in approval workflows for non-standard pricing.

trigger_events.description: Fired when a Opportunity is requires quote. Publisher domain owns the state transition; subscribers may react by creating downstream artifacts.

handoffs.description: New approved template available to CPQ for contract-draft generation.

trigger_events.description: A new contract template has been published. CPQ and CLM authoring tools can use; legal reviews any open quotes that should re-template.

handoffs.description: Materialization failure forces BI dashboards to fall back to live query with cost/latency impact.

trigger_events.description: Materialization refresh job failed; consumers fall back to live query with cost/latency hit.

handoffs.description: When a metric definition is certified in the metrics layer, BI tools that consume via SQL/REST need to refresh their cached schema and dashboard definitions. Mainstream BI tools all integrate via vendor-specific connectors, the protocol exists, but per-tool drift in semantic interpretation is the friction source.
handoffs.notes: Medium friction. The newer metrics-layer / BI integrations are stable; the broken state is when BI tools also author local metrics that diverge from the central definitions.

trigger_events.description: A metric definition completes its review/approval workflow and becomes the canonical version consumed downstream. Triggers BI cache invalidation, AI-agent definition refresh, and notification of metric consumers.

handoffs.description: Revocation surfaces warnings on BI dashboards consuming the asset.

trigger_events.description: Asset certification withdrawn due to quality or policy issue; consumers see warning.

handoffs.description: Updated metric access policy revalidates dashboard authorization and may hide affected tiles.

trigger_events.description: Access policy for a metric was modified; affected BI dashboards and AI agents revalidate authorization.

handoffs.description: Semantic-layer publication propagates to BI tools so dashboards use the canonical schema.

trigger_events.description: A new dimensional model (cube/semantic model) is published; BI tools and AI agents can pick up the schema.

handoffs.description: A metric defined in the platform's semantic layer is published for BI consumption. Each downstream BI tool re-imports or re-models the metric in its own semantic format; definitions drift, names collide, and the same metric name ends up disagreeing across BI tools even when both originated in the same platform metric. Identity reconciliation across systems pattern.
handoffs.notes: Convergence is partially solved within single-vendor stacks but breaks at vendor boundaries.

trigger_events.description: Fired when a Semantic Metric is published. Publisher domain owns the state transition; subscribers may react by creating downstream artifacts.
A real-time huddle/voice session begins. CCAAS-style recording rules may apply; calendar holds may be reconciled.
An external guest is invited to a WSC workspace or channel. IGA approves the cross-tenant access; DLP applies external-share policy; COLLAB-GOV logs the invite.

handoffs.description: Automations post status updates and task notifications into workstream collaboration channels.
handoffs.notes: source NULL until WORK-MGMT is modularized; target NULL until WSC declares a consumer DMDO on work_automations

trigger_events.description: A WORK-MGMT automation rule fired and produced downstream task effects. Generic signal for cross-tool task mirroring.

handoffs.description: Workload degradation signals propagate up to the owning PaaS app for self-healing or rollback.

trigger_events.description: A container workload has entered a degraded state (crash-looping pods, OOM-kills, readiness-probe failures). OBS opens an incident; ITSM creates a ticket.

handoffs.description: VSDP deployment completion confirms the PaaS app version is live; runtime can update environment markers.

trigger_events.description: A software deployment has completed to a target environment. OBS captures deployment marker; ITSM records the change; FINOPS picks up cost impact.

handoffs.description: Published low-code app deploys to the PaaS runtime hosting layer.

trigger_events.description: A low-code app is published to production; APP-PAAS hosts runtime, IPAAS may need to refresh integrations.

handoffs.description: Unpublish in HCMS triggers DXP cache purge and removal of any rendered surfaces that referenced the entry.

trigger_events.description: A previously published HCMS entry is withdrawn. DXP and any consuming channels invalidate caches and remove references.

handoffs.description: A11y findings on DXP-managed pages are written back as remediation tasks against the publishing surface owner.

trigger_events.description: An a11y scan finds a WCAG violation on a live surface. DXP/HCMS owners get a remediation task; legal/compliance is notified for high-severity issues.

handoffs.description: DXP publishes marketing pages, docs, and in-product release notes for the new feature.

trigger_events.description: A product feature has shipped to general availability. DXP needs marketing-page updates; CRM updates entitlements; CDP refreshes segment definitions that key on feature usage.

handoffs.description: Scheduled CMS release triggers a build pipeline ahead of go-live time so the rendered frontend is ready when the release publishes. SSG/ISR build kickoff via webhook. Failure modes: build pipeline runs against partial release content; release time changes don't re-trigger the build.

trigger_events.description: Fired when a Content Release is scheduled. Publisher domain owns the state transition; subscribers may react by creating downstream artifacts.

handoffs.description: HCMS publishes a content entry; DXP must re-render the affected pages, invalidate its CDN cache, or trigger an ISR rebuild. Payload typically includes content_type, entry_id, locale, and changed fields. Low friction when DXP and HCMS are the same vendor's integrated stack; bespoke and medium-friction when HCMS and DXP are from different vendors.

trigger_events.description: Fired when a Content Entry is published. Publisher domain owns the state transition; subscribers may react by creating downstream artifacts.

handoffs.description: Headless CMS publish webhook notifies DXP to invalidate caches and rebuild SSG/SSR routes for the affected entries.

trigger_events.description: Fired when a Content Release is published. Publisher domain owns the state transition; subscribers may react by creating downstream artifacts.

handoffs.description: HCMS schedules a future publish; DXP receives the embargo so it can pre-warm caches and stage the publish at the exact moment.

trigger_events.description: A content entry is scheduled for future publish. DXP and B2C-COMM register the embargo and prepare cache warming.

handoffs.description: DXP publishes release notes, updates docs, and runs the launch content; the cadence has to match the actual ship date.

trigger_events.description: A product release has been deployed to GA. DXP publishes release notes; CSM packages the customer communication; CRM updates entitled-features; CDP refreshes segments based on new capabilities.
