handoffs.description: Technical SEO findings (LCP, canonical, meta) are written back against the DXP page for owner remediation.

trigger_events.description: A technical SEO issue is detected (missing meta, slow LCP, duplicate canonicals). DXP/HCMS owners get a remediation task; PROD-MGMT may pick up for roadmap.

handoffs.description: Field renames, type changes, or removals on content_types break frontend renderers that are coupled to the schema. Typically handled through dev coordination (PR + deploy) rather than event-driven propagation. Cross-vendor stack with same logical entity pattern: the CMS schema and the frontend's TypeScript types must move together but live in different repos / different vendor tools.

trigger_events.description: Fired when a Content Type is changed. Publisher domain owns the state transition; subscribers may react by creating downstream artifacts.

handoffs.description: DXP updates the customer-facing roadmap page / portal so external messaging matches internal commitments.

trigger_events.description: A new product-roadmap version has been published. DXP updates customer-facing roadmap; CRM/CSM refresh narrative for renewal and expansion conversations.

handoffs.description: LOYALTY increments customer points, applies tier benefits, triggers reward offers.

trigger_events.description: Order created from checkout; cart → order_lines conversion complete.

handoffs.description: Activated segments inform loyalty tier and reward targeting. Friction when CDP segment definitions don't match loyalty schema.

trigger_events.description: Fired when a Audience Segment is activated. Publisher domain owns the state transition; subscribers may react by creating downstream artifacts.

handoffs.description: Delivered fulfillment triggers loyalty-point accrual.

trigger_events.description: Fulfillment confirmed delivered. Revenue recognition triggers in ERP-FIN; LOYALTY accrues points; review-request campaign may launch.

handoffs.description: Expired credentials toward APIM-managed APIs trigger renewal workflows.

trigger_events.description: An iPaaS connector's stored credential (OAuth refresh token, API key, service-account password) has expired or is about to expire. ITSM raises a renewal request; IGA captures the access change.

handoffs.description: A committed feature flows from agile planning into the delivery toolchain for implementation; teams reconcile feature state between the planning tool and the delivery tools, a frequent source of drift.

trigger_events.description: A feature has been committed to delivery and pulled into implementation.

handoffs.description: Published recipes link to the originating VSDP commit/release for traceability.

trigger_events.description: A new iPaaS integration recipe has been published and is available for execution. Downstream systems may subscribe to its trigger.

handoffs.description: PaaS deployment events cross-link to VSDP deployment records for unified delivery visibility.

trigger_events.description: A PaaS deployment completed successfully. Triggers OBS baseline refresh, KUBE-PLAT workload reconciliation, VSDP deployment-record cross-link.

handoffs.description: Build failures cross-link back to the originating VSDP commit for developer visibility.

trigger_events.description: A PaaS build pipeline failed (compile, test, or container-build stage). VSDP marks the commit as failing; TEST-MGMT picks up failed-test signals.

handoffs.description: Helm releases cross-link to VSDP deployment records for unified release tracking.

trigger_events.description: A Helm release has been installed or upgraded successfully on a cluster. VSDP cross-links the release; OBS rebaselines.

handoffs.description: Failed test runs block VSDP release gates and surface in delivery dashboards.

trigger_events.description: A test run failed (one or more failing test cases). Defects are created; release may be blocked.

handoffs.description: New OBS error signatures auto-create VSDP defect tickets linked to recent deployments.

trigger_events.description: OBS error tracking detected a new error signature (not seen before). ITSM/VSDP creates investigation ticket linked to recent release.

handoffs.description: OBS regression detection cues VSDP rollback or hotfix in delivery pipeline.

trigger_events.description: OBS error tracking detected a previously resolved error has regressed after a new deployment. VSDP may roll back; ITSM ticket.

handoffs.description: Cross-initiative dependencies often require manual delivery-team sequencing; tooling rarely auto-coordinates.

trigger_events.description: SPM identified a new cross-initiative dependency. WORK-MGMT and VSDP need visibility for sequencing; PSA captures for resourcing impact.

handoffs.description: APIM publishes deployment events; VSDP records them as release artifacts in the value stream.

trigger_events.description: An API has been deployed to a gateway environment. Triggers VSDP release-record creation, IPAAS endpoint refresh, OBS instrumentation.

handoffs.description: Test results gate VSDP pipeline progression and release decisions.

trigger_events.description: A test run completed (full pass/fail report available). VSDP gates the release; defects published downstream.

handoffs.description: PaaS app deployments materialize as workloads on the underlying Kubernetes platform.

trigger_events.description: A PaaS deployment completed successfully. Triggers OBS baseline refresh, KUBE-PLAT workload reconciliation, VSDP deployment-record cross-link.

handoffs.description: Degraded SaaS performance correlates with DEM endpoint signals for user-impact analysis.

trigger_events.description: NPMD detected degraded SaaS application performance from the user perspective. DEM cross-references endpoint signals; ITSM may auto-ticket.

handoffs.description: PO for a SaaS subscription creates the corresponding subscription record in SMP. Friction sits in matching the PO line items to a known SaaS app in the SMP catalog; new vendors require manual creation.

trigger_events.description: Fired when a SaaS Subscription is saas subscription created. Publisher domain owns the state transition; subscribers may react by creating downstream artifacts.

handoffs.description: A rightsizing or downgrade recommendation feeds the renewal engagement decision.

trigger_events.description: A new optimization recommendation generated by SMP.

handoffs.description: When APM marks an application for elimination or retirement (TIME 'Eliminate'), SMP cancels the corresponding SaaS subscription(s) to stop the spend and triggers deprovisioning. High friction: the portfolio-level decision must reconcile to the specific SaaS subscription(s) to cancel, and the cancellation must complete or the org keeps paying for a retired app.

trigger_events.description: Lifecycle transition (plan/develop/operate/sunset).

handoffs.description: Deprovisioning an application reclaims all of its license seat assignments.

trigger_events.description: A SaaS application has been deprovisioned tenant-wide. ITSM closes related tickets; IGA revokes; FINOPS terminates spend.

handoffs.description: A sanctioned SaaS application becomes eligible for license seat provisioning and usage metering in the optimization module.

trigger_events.description: A SaaS application has been sanctioned by IT. IGA establishes provisioning; FINOPS picks up spend; ITAM records subscription.

handoffs.description: Canceling a subscription triggers reclamation of its license seats.

trigger_events.description: Subscription terminated. Triggers deprovisioning across IGA, FINOPS, ITAM.

handoffs.description: Publishing an app to the self-service catalog opens employee app-access requests in the automation module.

trigger_events.description: A catalog listing is published and visible to employees for requests.

handoffs.description: Fulfilling a self-service app request provisions a license seat assignment.

trigger_events.description: Request fulfilled; user has access.

handoffs.description: Renewed SaaS contract in CLM updates the corresponding subscription in SMP with new term, new seat count, new pricing.

trigger_events.description: Fired when a Contract is renewed. Publisher domain owns the state transition; subscribers may react by creating downstream artifacts.

handoffs.description: SSO logs reveal a login to a SaaS app that's not in the sanctioned catalog — flagged as shadow IT. Complements the EXPENSE-side detection: SSO catches apps that use corporate SSO but aren't tracked; expense catches credit-card paid apps that don't.

trigger_events.description: Fired when a Shadow IT App is unsanctioned app. Publisher domain owns the state transition; subscribers may react by creating downstream artifacts.

handoffs.description: SaaS purchases on corporate cards reveal shadow IT to SMP — merchant categorization required to identify SaaS subscriptions vs other spend, then deduplicated against the existing SMP saas_subscription catalog. The card-side discovery path is the primary signal for off-procurement SaaS today. Shadow-data pattern.

trigger_events.description: Fired when a Card Transaction is posted. Publisher domain owns the state transition; subscribers may react by creating downstream artifacts.

handoffs.description: Corporate-card SaaS charge detected by the expense system surfaces a candidate shadow-IT app in SMP. High friction: finance sees the charge, IT/SMP sees (or doesn't see) the app — reconciling vendor-name-on-card with app-name-in-portfolio is messy and is one of the highest-value SMP-to-EXPENSE integrations.

trigger_events.description: Fired when a Shadow IT App is saas charge detected. Publisher domain owns the state transition; subscribers may react by creating downstream artifacts.

handoffs.description: A vendor risk assessment requiring remediation raises a portfolio alert on the application.

trigger_events.description: Risk findings require remediation before renewal can proceed.

handoffs.description: Customer/supplier/product golden records mastered in the MDM hub are projected into the lakehouse as platform-side data products; conversely, the platform's analytical resolution often produces a higher-quality match than the operational MDM hub. Who's authoritative? Most enterprises end up with a bidirectional batch sync where neither side fully trusts the other. Cross-vendor stack with same logical entity pattern.
handoffs.notes: Often the trigger for an MDM-modernization project that ends up moving golden-record mastery onto the platform itself.

trigger_events.description: Fired when a Data Product is synced. Publisher domain owns the state transition; subscribers may react by creating downstream artifacts.

handoffs.description: Identity-graph updates need reconciliation with MDM customer golden records. Notoriously high-friction: CDP's probabilistic matches vs MDM's deterministic survivorship rules.

trigger_events.description: CDP identity graph has resolved new edges (cookie merge, device match, email-to-known-customer). MA and LOYALTY refresh audience membership; CSM updates contact lookup.

handoffs.description: Lineage and run-stats published to catalog for impact analysis.

trigger_events.description: Data pipeline run completed successfully; downstream consumers can refresh; DCG receives lineage update.

handoffs.description: Published report registers as a downstream consumer in the catalog with lineage to underlying queries.

trigger_events.description: A BI report has been published and made available to subscribers; cache warm-up and notification dispatch follows.

handoffs.description: DSPM-discovered DB lands in DCG catalog.

trigger_events.description: DSPM finds new cloud database.

handoffs.description: A new data product is published on the platform: schema, owner, SLA, lineage. The enterprise data catalog needs to register it, attach glossary terms, surface stewardship workflows, and propagate lineage upstream. Lineage formats differ per platform (OpenLineage, proprietary), enterprise catalogs maintain their own model; sync is bespoke. Cross-vendor stack with same logical entity pattern.
handoffs.notes: Open standards (OpenLineage, Iceberg metadata, Polaris) are reducing this friction but most enterprises still hand-roll the bridge.

trigger_events.description: Fired when a Data Product is published. Publisher domain owns the state transition; subscribers may react by creating downstream artifacts.

handoffs.description: Catalog registers the feature set as a managed data asset with lineage to upstream tables.

trigger_events.description: A feature set is published to the feature store and available for online/offline serving; downstream models can subscribe.

handoffs.description: Captured query lineage published to the catalog for impact analysis.

trigger_events.description: A query lineage record is captured; downstream catalog and governance tooling ingests for impact analysis.

handoffs.description: Entity merge cascades to catalog glossary terms and related data assets.

trigger_events.description: Two KG entities merged after duplicate resolution; downstream relationships re-pointed.

handoffs.description: New KG entity becomes a glossary candidate for the catalog.

trigger_events.description: A new entity asserted in the KG; semantic index updates for retrieval and AI grounding.

handoffs.description: Schema crawler publishes new table; DCG auto-creates draft asset.

trigger_events.description: New table/dataset/API detected via automated crawler; DCG creates draft asset.

handoffs.description: BI publishes a dashboard; DCG ingests the new content for catalog discovery and governance metadata.

trigger_events.description: A new BI dashboard published to a workspace; access policies applied; subscribers notified.

handoffs.description: Aggregated stats published back to DCG as asset metadata.

trigger_events.description: Profile scan complete; triggers scorecard aggregation.

handoffs.description: DSPM propagates newly-discovered data-asset sensitivity labels to DCG.

trigger_events.description: Sensitivity label applied; DLP/DSPM react to enforce/audit.

handoffs.description: Newly deployed model registers lineage (feature inputs, training datasets) with the catalog.

trigger_events.description: An ML model is promoted from staging to production; triggers monitoring, lineage registration, and AI-agent tool-cache refresh.

handoffs.description: Low-code business-object schema change publishes lineage and schema update to catalog.

trigger_events.description: A low-code business object schema changed; dependent pages, workflows, integrations need re-validation.

handoffs.description: DQ breach surfaces on catalog asset page as a trust signal.

trigger_events.description: Data-quality dimension score (completeness, accuracy, timeliness, validity, uniqueness) crossed below threshold; incident raised.

handoffs.description: Published merge rule registered with catalog as a governance artifact.

trigger_events.description: A new MDM merge rule is published; pending duplicate sets re-evaluated against the rule.

handoffs.description: Pipeline SLA breach triggers DQ freshness incident on downstream assets.

trigger_events.description: Pipeline run exceeded SLA window; downstream freshness commitments at risk.

handoffs.description: Certification grant activates DQ SLAs and monitors for the asset.

trigger_events.description: Asset receives a certification level (gold/silver/bronze); consumers see trust signal.

handoffs.description: Feature freshness SLA breach raises a DQ incident on the underlying source pipeline.

trigger_events.description: Feature freshness SLA breached; serving features are older than tolerance window.

handoffs.description: Asset certified → DQ activates monitoring rules.

trigger_events.description: Steward approves asset for production; signals DQ to activate monitoring.

handoffs.description: A platform-native quality check on a lakehouse table fails. The enterprise DQ tool needs the finding to feed its central scorecard and ticketing. Two parallel quality systems exist; reconciliation is manual or via webhooks.

trigger_events.description: Fired when a Lakehouse Table is failed. Publisher domain owns the state transition; subscribers may react by creating downstream artifacts.

handoffs.description: Uncertain classification routed to records manager for human disposition.

trigger_events.description: Document classifier confidence below threshold; routed to fallback queue or human triage.

handoffs.description: Issued advice memos are filed in the privileged ECM repository with appropriate legal-hold and access controls.

trigger_events.description: Formal legal advice has been issued by in-house counsel (privileged memo, policy interpretation, contract guidance). ECM files the privileged document; the requesting business function logs the guidance against their workflow.

handoffs.description: When a retention policy expires in ECM-RECORDS-GOV, the affected documents in ECM-REPOSITORY progress to disposition (superseded/archived) per the records schedule.

trigger_events.description: A document has reached the end of its retention period under policy. ECM proposes disposition; LSD intervenes for any holds; AUDIT receives the disposition evidence.

handoffs.description: Archiving a WSC channel triggers a final ECM capture pass of messages and attachments for record-keeping.
handoffs.notes: target NULL until ECM is modularized

trigger_events.description: A WSC channel is archived (read-only). ECM captures attachments for retention; IGA revokes ongoing access.

handoffs.description: WSC attachments in regulated channels are captured to ECM for retention and discoverability.
handoffs.notes: target NULL until ECM is modularized

trigger_events.description: A file is attached to a chat message. DLP inspects; ECM may capture an authoritative copy; DAM is notified if the attachment is a brand asset.

handoffs.description: E-discovery requires ECM collection workflows for in-scope content.

trigger_events.description: An e-discovery request has been created. Triggers ECM collection, processing, and review workflow.

handoffs.description: New matter triggers ECM matter-workspace provisioning.

trigger_events.description: Legal matter has been formally opened after conflict-check clearance and engagement-letter execution; triggers calendar setup, trust-deposit collection, and matter-team assignment.

handoffs.description: Court filings archived to ECM matter workspace for record retention.
handoffs.notes: target NULL until ECM is modularized

trigger_events.description: A court filing has been submitted on behalf of a client. Triggers ECM archive, billing capture, deadline tracking.

handoffs.description: Completed extracted record stored in ECM with metadata indexed for retrieval.

trigger_events.description: Document extraction complete and validated; downstream record creation in AP-AUTO/ECM.

handoffs.description: Legal hold freezes ECM retention policies on identified content and custodians.

trigger_events.description: A legal hold has been issued. Triggers custodian notification, ECM retention freeze, HCM-aware preservation.

handoffs.description: Opening a matter provisions a privileged ECM workspace where pleadings, correspondence, and work-product are filed under legal hold.

trigger_events.description: A new in-house legal matter has been opened (litigation hold, regulatory enquiry, M&A workstream, employment dispute). ECM creates the matter file workspace; GRC logs the regulatory or risk linkage.

handoffs.description: Authoring a content entry resolves asset references from DAM; missing or unapproved assets block publish.

trigger_events.description: A new HCMS entry is authored as a draft. Editorial workflow picks it up for review routing.

handoffs.description: Final-approved creative deliverable registers in DAM as the canonical brand asset with metadata (client, campaign, agency_job, usage rights, expiry). Surfaces in DAM search for future reuse.
handoffs.notes: Friction shape: cross-vendor stack — agency mgmt and DAM are usually different vendors; manual metadata enrichment is common before the asset is genuinely findable.

trigger_events.description: All client and internal reviewers have approved the final version of a creative deliverable; ready to register in DAM as the canonical brand asset.

handoffs.description: DAM publishes an approved asset; HCMS authors need the asset to appear in their picker for inclusion in content entries. Integration typically resolves asset URLs at content delivery time, so DAM URL rotation, taxonomy renames, or rights-revocations break already-published HCMS entries downstream. Identity-reconciliation pattern: same asset, different identifier spaces across DAM and HCMS, no canonical resolver in most stacks.

trigger_events.description: Fired when a Digital Asset is published. Publisher domain owns the state transition; subscribers may react by creating downstream artifacts.

handoffs.description: Brand/voice violations are routed back to the originating HCMS entry as an author task before re-publish.

trigger_events.description: A WEB-CONTOPS brand or voice scanner flags non-compliant copy. HCMS author and brand-governance owner receive review tasks.

handoffs.description: Broken links found in published surfaces are written back as fix tasks on the source HCMS entry.

trigger_events.description: WEB-CONTOPS link crawler finds a broken outbound or inbound link. DXP/HCMS authors receive a remediation task; SEO scorecards update.

handoffs.description: A waiver is sent to the e-signature provider for the participant to sign; the signed release is returned and attached to the booking.

trigger_events.description: A waiver is dispatched to a participant for electronic signature via the e-signature provider.

handoffs.description: Recomputed lead score reaching engagement threshold triggers sales-engagement cadence enrollment.

trigger_events.description: Lead score has been recalculated based on new engagement or fit data. CRM may re-route the lead; SALES-ENG may pick it up for cadence.

handoffs.description: New opportunity assignment in CRM auto-enrolls the contact in the appropriate cadence in SALES-ENG. Friction sits in cadence-selection rules (which cadence for which deal type, region, segment) which drift faster than the integration code.

trigger_events.description: Fired when a Opportunity is assigned. Publisher domain owns the state transition; subscribers may react by creating downstream artifacts.

handoffs.description: A lead's predictive score has crossed the qualified-handoff threshold; SALES-ENG picks up for cadence enrollment. Failure modes: noisy scoring causes cadence whiplash; threshold tuned per segment but not surfaced.
handoffs.notes: Probabilistic-to-deterministic shape: scoring is heuristic, action is binding (enroll in cadence).

trigger_events.description: A lead's predictive score has crossed the qualified-handoff threshold. Sales engagement should pick it up for an outreach cadence.

handoffs.description: Whitespace (cross-sell / upsell) feeds SALES-ENG for prospecting. Failure modes: account-team toes; whitespace not synchronized with existing CSM relationships.
handoffs.notes: Probabilistic identification meets coordinated outreach.

trigger_events.description: Strategic account planning has identified whitespace (cross-sell or upsell opportunity not yet pursued). Sales engagement picks up for prospecting.

handoffs.description: CDP-detected high-intent signal (pricing-page revisits, integration-doc views, competitor-comparison engagement) triggers cadence enrollment in SALES-ENG so reps reach out at the right moment. High friction: the intent signal is probabilistic, the cadence enrollment rules are rep-team-specific, and the systems have very different data models. The marquee 'intent data → outreach' handoff that powers modern outbound.

trigger_events.description: Fired when a Cadence is detected. Publisher domain owns the state transition; subscribers may react by creating downstream artifacts.

handoffs.description: An invoice clearing returns the subscription from past-due to active so the customer regains normal service.

trigger_events.description: Customer invoice has been fully paid. ERP-FIN applies cash; CSM gets a healthy-account signal; LOYALTY accrues points where applicable.

handoffs.description: Depleted entitlement triggers overage-billing review in SUB-MGMT.

trigger_events.description: Customer has consumed all units of an entitlement (e.g. support hours, included incidents). CSM should engage for overage discussion; SUB-MGMT may trigger overage billing.

handoffs.description: Detecting metered overage triggers an overage line on the upcoming invoice so usage above plan is billed.

trigger_events.description: Posted usage exceeds the subscription's included tier. SUB-MGMT triggers overage billing; CSM may engage for tier upgrade conversation.

handoffs.description: Activating a subscription triggers the first invoice so billing begins as soon as the customer is live.

trigger_events.description: Fired when a Customer Subscription is activated. Publisher domain owns the state transition; subscribers may react by creating downstream artifacts.

handoffs.description: Declining customer health score flags renewal risk; SUB-MGMT may need to adjust dunning lenience or surface for retention. Failure modes: multiple health-score variants disagree.
handoffs.notes: Probabilistic-to-deterministic shape.

trigger_events.description: A customer's composite health score has declined materially. CSM needs retention motion; SUB-MGMT needs to flag for renewal risk.

handoffs.description: A dunning escalation feeds the subscription into a suspended state when collection attempts on the overdue balance fail.

trigger_events.description: A dunning sequence has escalated to the next severity tier (e.g. payment retry N exhausted, account suspension imminent). CSM and collections need a heads-up for retention or contact.

handoffs.description: Completed orchestrations that meter billable activity feed subscription and usage metering downstream.

trigger_events.description: A process instance finished its end event. Carries the instance id, definition key, and final variables; downstream domains react to the business outcome.

handoffs.description: A renewal coming due triggers the recurring invoice run so the next billing period is invoiced on time.

trigger_events.description: A subscription is within the renewal window (typically 90 days from term end). CSM should engage with the customer for renewal motion.

handoffs.description: Signed contract creates the customer subscription in SUB-MGMT: plan, term, MRR/ARR, billing cadence, seat count, start date. The 'order-to-active' moment.

trigger_events.description: Fired when a Contract is signed. Publisher domain owns the state transition; subscribers may react by creating downstream artifacts.

handoffs.description: Storefront order containing a subscription SKU creates the customer_subscription in SUB-MGMT, bypassing the CPQ/CLM path used for B2B deals.

trigger_events.description: Fired when a Customer Subscription is subscription purchase. Publisher domain owns the state transition; subscribers may react by creating downstream artifacts.

handoffs.description: CSM-side churn-risk detection (case patterns, low CSAT, low product usage) feeds back to SUB-MGMT to influence dunning treatment, retention offers, and renewal forecasting. High friction because the churn-risk model rarely lives in SUB-MGMT's data model, requiring an event-driven adapter.

trigger_events.description: Fired when a Dunning Event is churn risk detected. Publisher domain owns the state transition; subscribers may react by creating downstream artifacts.

handoffs.description: Recipient bounce or address failure on a subscription is logged for user-account follow-up.

trigger_events.description: Scheduled subscription delivery (email, chat channel, file) failed for a recipient; needs retry or address fix.

handoffs.description: Quota overages feed subscription billing for overage charges.

trigger_events.description: An API consumer has exceeded its provisioned quota or rate-limit window. SUB-MGMT may trigger overage billing; SECOPS evaluates for abuse.

handoffs.description: Confirmed churn triggers SUB-MGMT subscription cancellation and revenue-impact recognition. Failure modes: churn confirmed but contract-end-date not aligned; refund logic edge cases.
handoffs.notes: Leaver recall: the going-away event must reliably reach finance to avoid continued billing.

trigger_events.description: Customer churn has been confirmed (subscription cancel, account close, contract non-renewal). SUB-MGMT processes the cancellation; CRM marks the account; LOYALTY revokes tier benefits if applicable.

handoffs.description: CSM-identified expansion needs SUB-MGMT proposal generation and CRM opportunity creation. Failure modes: duplicate opportunities when CSM and sales both file.
handoffs.notes: Tight cross-domain coordination.

trigger_events.description: CSM has identified an expansion opportunity (more seats, additional modules, tier upgrade). SUB-MGMT prepares the proposal; CRM creates the expansion opportunity.

handoffs.description: An invoice going past due drives the subscription into a past-due state so access and renewal decisions reflect the unpaid balance.

trigger_events.description: Customer invoice is past due. Dunning workflow starts; CSM is notified for retention; ERP-FIN updates aging buckets.

handoffs.description: Published to billing for invoice/subscription account reconciliation.

trigger_events.description: New deduplicated customer golden record resolved; published to CRM/CSM/SUB-MGMT/CDP.

handoffs.description: SUB-MGMT consumes one-off orders that are part of subscription replenishment rhythm.

trigger_events.description: Order created from checkout; cart → order_lines conversion complete.

handoffs.description: Signed contract triggers SUB-MGMT to activate the subscription record.

trigger_events.description: Fired when a Contract is signed. Publisher domain owns the state transition; subscribers may react by creating downstream artifacts.

handoffs.description: Closed-won opportunity triggers subscription creation. SUB-MGMT picks up quote terms via contract; mismatched product catalogs cause provisioning errors.

trigger_events.description: Fired when a Opportunity is closed won. Publisher domain owns the state transition; subscribers may react by creating downstream artifacts.

handoffs.description: Accepted quote with subscription terms triggers SUB-MGMT to provision the subscription record.

trigger_events.description: Buyer has accepted the quote (typically via e-sign or portal acceptance). CLM creates the contract draft; CRM advances opportunity to closed-won pending signature; SUB-MGMT prepares subscription provisioning.

handoffs.description: Published bot definition routed in CCAAS channels for new conversations.

trigger_events.description: Conversational bot definition published; CCAAS and CSM channels route to new version.

handoffs.description: Customer-facing chat threads escalated for live assist hand off to CCAAS with full transcript context.
handoffs.notes: target NULL until CCAAS is modularized

trigger_events.description: A WSC thread is converted into a support ticket. ITSM/CSM/HRSD open a case with the thread transcript attached.

handoffs.description: Updated KB articles re-index in contact-center agent desktop and bot grounding.

trigger_events.description: KB article major version published; AI search indexes and embeddings need refresh.

handoffs.description: Bot fallback hands the conversation off to a human agent with full transcript context.

trigger_events.description: Bot fell back to fallback or human-handoff branch; KMS gap may be surfaced.

handoffs.description: Bot-to-human handoff passes the conversation transcript and context to CCAAS. Failure modes: transcript context truncated by agent UI; customer has to repeat.
handoffs.notes: Identity reconciliation needed across CONV-AI and CCAAS user sessions.

trigger_events.description: A bot conversation has been handed off to a human agent. CCAAS picks up with full transcript context.

handoffs.description: Hired candidate drives onboarding-plan kickoff with role/location/manager context from ATS payload.

trigger_events.description: Fired when a Candidate is hired. Publisher domain owns the state transition; subscribers may react by creating downstream artifacts.

handoffs.notes: Plan activation schedules the welcome cadence and pairs a buddy; intra-domain progression.

trigger_events.description: Onboarding plan template instantiated for a new hire. Tasks generated; cross-domain provisioning subscriptions can fire.

handoffs.notes: cross | ATS->ONBOARDING | rescind recalls the onboarding journey if already spawned

trigger_events.description: Fired when an offer is rescinded after extension. Subscribers cancel the background check, halt the pre-employee onboarding paperwork, recall the onboarding journey, withdraw benefit enrollment, and unwind compensation seeding.

handoffs.notes: Plan activation seeds a document_collection for the journey; intra-domain progression, no out-of-process message.

trigger_events.description: Onboarding plan template instantiated for a new hire. Tasks generated; cross-domain provisioning subscriptions can fire.

handoffs.description: Candidate accepts offer in ATS; ATS publishes the offer-accepted event with offer details, position, hiring manager, location, start date. Onboarding instantiates a journey by selecting a plan based on role + location + employment type, materializes the task list, and notifies the new hire to begin pre-boarding. Failure modes: late offer-detail changes after journey instantiation (start date pushed, role re-leveled) require either journey re-materialization or manual reconciliation.

trigger_events.description: Fired when a Offer is accepted. Publisher domain owns the state transition; subscribers may react by creating downstream artifacts.

handoffs.notes: Welcome communication sent advances the journey's pre-board stage.

trigger_events.description: Pre-boarding welcome email/packet dispatched. Day-one no-show risk reduced; engagement signal captured.

handoffs.notes: Doc collection completion unblocks day-one transition on the journey.

trigger_events.description: All required new-hire documents (I-9, tax forms, direct-deposit, NDA) collected and validated. Payroll and IGA can finalize setup.

handoffs.description: HCM creates the canonical employee record (typically on or near Day-1, or earlier for pre-boarding access). Onboarding binds the journey to the new employee_id so task ownership and reminders route to the right user portal. Lower friction when ATS and HCM are the same vendor; higher when they're separate.

trigger_events.description: Fired when a Employee is created. Publisher domain owns the state transition; subscribers may react by creating downstream artifacts.

handoffs.notes: Buddy assignment active marks pre-board stage progress on the journey.

trigger_events.description: Buddy/mentor assignment activated (moves from 'assigned' to 'active'). WSC channel provisioning and intro-meeting scheduling trigger.

handoffs.description: Rolling forecast refresh in EPM (typically monthly or quarterly) triggers SWP to re-evaluate plan assumptions and scenarios. Distinct from the annual budget.cycle_started trigger — this is the in-cycle refresh signal, finer-grained and lower friction.

trigger_events.description: Fired when a Forecast is refreshed. Publisher domain owns the state transition; subscribers may react by creating downstream artifacts.

handoffs.description: Identified skill gaps feed the strategic workforce plan to inform hire-vs-train-vs-contract decisions for the practice.

trigger_events.description: Aggregate skill inventory across the practice shows a gap against forecast demand (specific certification, technology, or role family). SWP triggers a hire-vs-train decision; LMS may seed an upskilling plan.

handoffs.description: Segment-composition shift updates SWP plan assumptions on demand, supply, and natural reduction.

trigger_events.description: Workforce-segment composition crossed a meaningful threshold (representation, span-of-control, attrition). Downstream DEI and HCM dashboards re-render; SWP recalibrates plan assumptions.

handoffs.description: SPM books person/team; SWP syncs to workforce plan and decrements available capacity.

trigger_events.description: Tentative allocation becomes binding.

handoffs.description: Adopted scenario triggers a cost-projection recompute under the new headcount and org-design assumptions.

trigger_events.description: Executive workforce scenario chosen (growth, restructure, shore-shift). HCM org changes, ATS hiring plan, and EPM financial plan adopt scenario.

handoffs.description: Adopted scenario refreshes the headcount and position demand baseline; demand-forecast re-runs its plan under the chosen scenario.

trigger_events.description: Executive workforce scenario chosen (growth, restructure, shore-shift). HCM org changes, ATS hiring plan, and EPM financial plan adopt scenario.

handoffs.description: Filled requisition feeds SWP actuals-vs-plan reconciliation.

trigger_events.description: Fired when a Job Requisition is filled. Publisher domain owns the state transition; subscribers may react by creating downstream artifacts.

handoffs.description: Filled requisitions from ATS decrement open demand in SWP's position forecasts and update plan-vs-actual fill metrics (time-to-fill, fill rate by role/geo). Lower friction than headcount.actuals_updated from HCM because the requisition→forecast mapping is more direct.

trigger_events.description: Fired when a Job Requisition is filled. Publisher domain owns the state transition; subscribers may react by creating downstream artifacts.

handoffs.description: SWP reserves headcount from workforce_scenarios; demand > supply requires escalation.

trigger_events.description: Initiative moves to execution; announces to SWP (capacity) and WORK-MGMT (scope).

handoffs.description: Refreshed demand triggers supply reconciliation: supply-planning evaluates internal-mobility, retirement, and external-supply assumptions against the new demand baseline.

trigger_events.description: Workforce-plan refreshed demand by job family / location / quarter. ATS hiring plan and HCM headcount budget should align.

handoffs.description: Refreshed market medians feed strategic workforce-cost models and headcount planning scenarios.

trigger_events.description: External market-comp benchmark dataset refreshed. COMP-MGMT and SWP planning use updated medians; band updates may follow.

handoffs.description: Approved headcount triggers cost-projection refresh: cost-projections rolls the new requisition load into the loaded-comp envelope.

trigger_events.description: Fired when a Job Requisition is approved. Publisher domain owns the state transition; subscribers may react by creating downstream artifacts.

handoffs.description: Annual (or rolling) budget cycle in EPM triggers refresh of workforce plans aligned to the new budget envelope. SWP planners rebuild scenarios under updated cost ceilings. High friction because EPM and SWP rarely share a common plan structure (org-unit dimensions, time grain, account hierarchies all differ), forcing manual reconciliation and re-modeling.

trigger_events.description: Fired when a Budget is cycle started. Publisher domain owns the state transition; subscribers may react by creating downstream artifacts.

handoffs.description: Actual headcount changes (hires, terminations, transfers, leaves) from HCM flow to SWP for plan-vs-actual reconciliation. Usually nightly batch; some orgs run weekly. Friction sits in normalizing HCM's org structure to the planning structure SWP uses.

trigger_events.description: Fired when a Headcount Plan is actuals updated. Publisher domain owns the state transition; subscribers may react by creating downstream artifacts.

handoffs.description: People Analytics produces an attrition forecast (typically per org unit × tenure × performance band). SWP consumes the forecast to update plan assumptions on natural reduction, refining demand for backfill hires. Friction is medium — the forecast is well-defined but pushing it back into SWP scenarios requires manual planner judgment.

trigger_events.description: Fired when a Workforce Plan is forecast updated. Publisher domain owns the state transition; subscribers may react by creating downstream artifacts.

handoffs.description: Period actuals from WFM feed Strategic Workforce Planning plan-vs-actual. Coding mismatches between WFM cost-centers and SWP plan units cause reconciliation pain.

trigger_events.description: Fired when a Time Entry is posted. Publisher domain owns the state transition; subscribers may react by creating downstream artifacts.

handoffs.description: Released assignments return supply to the strategic workforce plan and are evaluated against forecast demand for re-deployment.

trigger_events.description: A resource rolls off a project (planned end reached, early release, or scope change). Returns capacity to the HCM bench, closes the WORK-MGMT seat, and may trigger SWP demand-replan.

handoffs.description: SWP workforce scenarios incorporate refreshed attrition baselines.

trigger_events.description: People-Analytics published refreshed attrition forecast. HCM and SWP align hiring plans; TALENT-MGMT prioritizes retention motion for at-risk segments.

handoffs.description: A WORK-MGMT automation rule has been disabled. PROD-MGMT subscribers stop reacting to its downstream effects (e.g. auto-creation of feature_request linkages from incoming work_items).

trigger_events.description: An automation rule has been disabled (manually, on error budget exhaustion, or by audit). Cascading downstream actions stop.

handoffs.description: Engineering team automations mirror into product-management roadmap tracking.

trigger_events.description: A WORK-MGMT automation rule fired and produced downstream task effects. Generic signal for cross-tool task mirroring.

handoffs.description: WM work_item completion updates PROD-MGMT roadmap progress when items are linked to feature_requests or product_releases. Most product-mgmt tools (Aha, Productboard, Roadmunk) integrate via this signal but each integration is bespoke — friction is the mapping between work_item id and roadmap_item id.

trigger_events.description: A work_item transitions to done/complete state in a WORK-MGMT platform. Used by SPM for portfolio rollup, by PSA for billable hours close-out, and by ITSM when the work_item was linked to an IT ticket.

handoffs.description: SPM closes roadmap item; PROD-MGMT marks feature shipped.

trigger_events.description: Feature/capability ships.

handoffs.description: An accepted feature_request flows from PM-DISCOVERY into PM-ROADMAP-DELIVERY, where a draft product_feature is created and slotted onto the roadmap.

trigger_events.description: A feature_request has been accepted into the roadmap. PROD-MGMT drafts a product_feature in PM-ROADMAP-DELIVERY and the request moves out of triage.

handoffs.description: When a product_feature is released in PM-ROADMAP-DELIVERY, PM-DISCOVERY closes the originating feature_request, completing the listen-build-close loop.

trigger_events.description: A product feature has shipped to general availability. DXP needs marketing-page updates; CRM updates entitlements; CDP refreshes segment definitions that key on feature usage.

handoffs.description: Team OKR commits in WM; PROD-MGMT roadmaps that align to OKR cycles pick up the committed objective for alignment scoring. Aha, Productboard, and similar tools maintain OKR sync as a paid feature.

trigger_events.description: A team-execution OKR is committed: KRs are finalized, owners set, and downstream task-creation / KR-to-task linking may now happen. Subscribers in TASK-EXEC create placeholder work_items or link existing ones to the freshly-committed KRs.

handoffs.description: BPA-side value-stream analysis surfaces a delivery bottleneck; product management consumes for prioritization. Today: meetings + slides. Failure modes: priorities not adjusted, no closed loop back to the value-stream artifact.

trigger_events.description: BPA's simulation or analysis identifies a bottleneck in a value stream — consumers (PROD-MGMT, etc.) re-prioritize.

handoffs.description: Identified bottlenecks feed product backlog with process-improvement work items.

trigger_events.description: A simulation run flagged a process bottleneck. PROD-MGMT and SPM consume for process-improvement prioritization.

handoffs.description: Winning A/B variant and lift metrics are recorded against the product roadmap item, closing the experiment loop in product management.

trigger_events.description: An A/B test reaches its planned sample or duration and a winner is declared. PROD-MGMT picks up the learning; the winning variant is promoted to default.

handoffs.description: When a customer_feedback_item is linked to a feature in PM-DISCOVERY, PM-ROADMAP-DELIVERY enriches the linked product_feature with the supporting demand signal.

trigger_events.description: A feedback item has been linked to a feature_request or product_feature, closing the listening loop. CSM/CRM should surface this on the customer record for renewal and expansion conversations.

handoffs.description: End-of-cycle OKR score feeds PROD-MGMT retrospective and next-cycle roadmap prioritization. Distinct from committed (kickoff) and aligned to roadmap delivery KPIs.

trigger_events.description: A team-execution OKR is scored at end-of-cycle. Scoring is the cadence ritual on the WORK-MGMT side (Asana / Monday / ClickUp Goals models); distinct from TALENT-MGMT-side grading which is tied to performance review compensation. Cascades to dependent work_items closure and dashboard rollup.

handoffs.description: Requirement-to-test linkage updates feed product traceability and coverage reports.

trigger_events.description: A requirement has been linked to a test case (or unlinked). Triggers traceability-matrix refresh and coverage-gap analysis.

handoffs.description: Merged PRs tied to feature requests update product roadmap delivery status.

trigger_events.description: A pull request has been merged to a tracked branch. Triggers CD pipeline kickoff, release-note generation, and traceability linkage.

handoffs.description: Account tier changes trigger territory or quota realignment. Failure modes: mid-quarter changes invalidate existing assignments; commission impact is retroactive.
handoffs.notes: Period-coupling shape: tier changes are felt at quota recalculation boundaries.

trigger_events.description: An account's tier classification (strategic / enterprise / mid-market / SMB) has changed. Triggers territory or quota realignment in sales performance and CSM re-segmentation.

handoffs.description: New opportunities feed pipeline quota tracking in SALES-PERF. Failure modes: rep-attribution edge cases (transfers, team deals).
handoffs.notes: Same-stack low-friction if SALES-PERF lives inside the CRM.

trigger_events.description: A new opportunity has been created. Feeds pipeline quota tracking in sales performance and forecast inputs in revenue intelligence.

handoffs.description: Pipeline health metrics dropping below threshold prompt sales leadership pipeline-build motion. Failure modes: lagging indicators trigger after the quarter is already lost.
handoffs.notes: Leadership-layer signal: REV-INTEL upward to SALES-PERF leadership.

trigger_events.description: Aggregate pipeline health metric has crossed below a configured threshold (coverage ratio, weighted forecast). Sales leadership needs visibility for pipeline-build motion.

handoffs.description: Recalculated deal-risk scores in REV-INTEL-DEAL-INTEL feed the forecast roll-up in REV-INTEL-FORECAST.

trigger_events.description: A deal's AI-derived risk score has been recalculated after new activity, conversation, or CRM signal. Forecast and pipeline-inspection surfaces re-read the score.

handoffs.description: Conversation insights published in REV-INTEL-CONVERSATION surface to REV-INTEL-COACHING so coaches can anchor sessions to the calls that matter.

trigger_events.description: Conversation intelligence has published an insight (competitor mention, pricing objection, churn risk, next-step commitment). Revenue intelligence and CRM consume for deal-risk and coaching.

handoffs.description: Auto-captured activities in REV-INTEL-ACTIVITY-CAPTURE feed deal scoring in REV-INTEL-DEAL-INTEL as engagement signal.

trigger_events.description: An email, call, or meeting has been auto-captured and attributed to an opportunity or account.

handoffs.description: Conversation insights published in REV-INTEL-CONVERSATION feed the deal-scoring model in REV-INTEL-DEAL-INTEL, updating risk scores from competitor mentions, objections, and sentiment.

trigger_events.description: Conversation intelligence has published an insight (competitor mention, pricing objection, churn risk, next-step commitment). Revenue intelligence and CRM consume for deal-risk and coaching.

handoffs.description: Stage changes feed revenue intelligence forecast model. Low friction: REV-INTEL is purpose-built for CRM-event ingest.

trigger_events.description: Fired when a Opportunity is stage changed. Publisher domain owns the state transition; subscribers may react by creating downstream artifacts.

handoffs.description: Paid social conversion / signal data flows to revenue intelligence for attribution, pipeline influence, and incrementality measurement.

trigger_events.description: A server-side conversion event was matched to paid social delivery. Downstream: attribution and incrementality, revenue analytics.

handoffs.description: High-intent signals feed revenue intelligence next-best-action recommendations.

trigger_events.description: Fired when a Cadence is detected. Publisher domain owns the state transition; subscribers may react by creating downstream artifacts.

handoffs.description: Closed-lost opportunities feed REV-INTEL for win-loss analysis. Failure modes: rep-entered loss reasons are free-text and inconsistent; lost-then-revived deals double-count.
handoffs.notes: Cross-vendor stack: REV-INTEL is often a distinct platform; identifier reconciliation is messy.

trigger_events.description: An opportunity has been marked closed-lost. Triggers win-loss analysis in revenue intelligence and re-engagement nurture in marketing.

handoffs.description: Conversation-intelligence insights flow to revenue-intelligence deal-risk model. Often the same vendor across both capabilities.

trigger_events.description: Conversation intelligence has published an insight (competitor mention, pricing objection, churn risk, next-step commitment). Revenue intelligence and CRM consume for deal-risk and coaching.

handoffs.description: Advocacy-driven reach and pipeline-attribution signals flow to Revenue Intelligence so social-selling activity by employees is captured against accounts and opportunities for revenue analysis.

trigger_events.description: Cumulative reach or earned media value from advocacy shares crosses a reporting threshold, signaling material program impact for revenue attribution.

handoffs.description: A filed lease disclosure feeds the consolidated financial statements and footnote package.

trigger_events.description: A lease-accounting disclosure has been finalized and filed for the reporting period.

handoffs.description: Employee-share reach and engagement metrics flow to Social Media Management so brand-channel social analytics can fold organic advocacy reach into total social attribution alongside owned-channel performance.

trigger_events.description: An employee share is successfully posted to a linked personal social account. Drives share-metric collection, points award, and downstream reach and attribution.

handoffs.description: A launched paid campaign gives organic social management context on what is being boosted / promoted so organic and paid stay aligned.

trigger_events.description: A paid social campaign moved live across its target ad platforms. Downstream: organic-side context in SMM, performance tracking begins.

handoffs.description: Published advocacy content is made available to Social Media Management so brand and influencer program teams can coordinate which curated assets employees and external creators amplify.

trigger_events.description: An approved advocacy content item is published to advocates and becomes shareable. Triggers newsletter inclusion and availability in advocate feeds.

handoffs.description: A frontline broadcast published to deskless workers is mirrored to the corporate communications platform so internal comms can see frontline reach alongside office-channel reach.

trigger_events.description: A frontline broadcast was published to its audience; downstream channels deliver it and acknowledgment tracking starts.

handoffs.description: Newly published pages are queued for an immediate WEB-CONTOPS audit (a11y, SEO, brand, broken links) so issues are caught fast.

trigger_events.description: A DXP web page transitions to published. Downstream caches invalidate, search indexers re-crawl, CDP/MA pick up new audience-targeting context, and WEB-CONTOPS schedules a fresh audit.

handoffs.description: Unpublishing a page closes any open WEB-CONTOPS findings and marks the lifecycle plan complete.

trigger_events.description: A web page is taken offline (sunset, expired, withdrawn). WEB-CONTOPS marks lifecycle plan complete and KMS removes any linked references.

handoffs.description: Adding a locale expands WEB-CONTOPS audit and accessibility scan scope to the new locale's published surfaces.

trigger_events.description: A new locale is enabled in HCMS. DXP provisions matching audience targeting; WEB-CONTOPS expands audit scope; translation vendors are engaged.

handoffs.description: An enterprise governance tool updates an access policy (tag-based, attribute-based, lineage-derived). The platform's native RBAC layer needs to enforce it. Policy syntax differs; not every governance assertion maps to a platform-native control; bridges are bespoke and drift over time. Identity reconciliation pattern in the access-control axis.
handoffs.notes: Standards (OpenPolicyAgent, ABAC profiles in lakehouses) reduce but don't eliminate the friction.

trigger_events.description: Fired when a Lakehouse Table is updated. Publisher domain owns the state transition; subscribers may react by creating downstream artifacts.

handoffs.description: Successful pipeline run signals downstream ML feature refresh.

trigger_events.description: Data pipeline run completed successfully; downstream consumers can refresh; DCG receives lineage update.

handoffs.description: Imported ontology reloads schema caches for AI agents grounded on the knowledge graph.

trigger_events.description: An external ontology has been imported and reconciled into the KG; mappings published to DCG and AI agents.

handoffs.description: Schema evolution signals downstream model and feature-set validation.

trigger_events.description: Schema version evolved (added/removed/changed fields); compatibility check and consumer notification.

handoffs.description: DQ breach on a feature source pauses dependent model training or serving.

trigger_events.description: Data-quality dimension score (completeness, accuracy, timeliness, validity, uniqueness) crossed below threshold; incident raised.

handoffs.description: AI agents on data-AI platforms ground LLM responses in metric definitions via tool-use APIs. When a metric is certified, the agent's tool catalog needs to update.
handoffs.notes: Medium friction. The 2024+ wedge for metrics-layer vendors: deterministic AI grounding requires fresh definitions and clean lineage. Vendor-specific connectors dominate, each metrics-layer vendor exposes its own LLM-facing API.

trigger_events.description: A metric definition completes its review/approval workflow and becomes the canonical version consumed downstream. Triggers BI cache invalidation, AI-agent definition refresh, and notification of metric consumers.

handoffs.description: A managed ingestion tool completes a load and signals the platform to refresh dependent pipelines and materializations. Mature pattern with first-class event integration in most lakehouse runtimes.

trigger_events.description: Fired when a Lakehouse Table is completed. Publisher domain owns the state transition; subscribers may react by creating downstream artifacts.

handoffs.description: Published ontology updates trigger AI agents that use the graph for grounded reasoning to refresh their tool / schema cache. Agent frameworks and vendor-specific agent runtimes consume KG schemas via SPARQL or REST.
handoffs.notes: Medium friction. The integration protocols exist; the friction is keeping agent schemas in sync with rapidly-iterating ontologies during AI-app development.

trigger_events.description: A new ontology version is published. Triggers ontology-reload in dependent KGP instances, federated SPARQL endpoint refresh, AI-agent schema-cache invalidation, and downstream consumers (DCG glossaries, MDM mappings) revalidation.

handoffs.description: Materialized metric refresh exposes new features/labels usable by AI agents and ML pipelines.

trigger_events.description: A pre-aggregated metric materialization is refreshed; BI caches invalidate; AI agents reload.

handoffs.description: A hardware asset retired/disposed in HAM should trigger RMM agent uninstall and license release to avoid orphaned agents continuing to phone home and consume seats. Failure modes: classic leaver-pattern friction — the 'going away' event reliably reaches HAM but doesn't reliably reach RMM; orphan agents accumulate; per-endpoint billing inflates.
handoffs.notes: Leaver / cancellation recall pattern; structural friction across the IT-ops cluster.

trigger_events.description: Fired when a RMM Agent is retired. Publisher domain owns the state transition; subscribers may react by creating downstream artifacts.
Monitoring alert breached a configured threshold. ITOM publishes; ITSM may auto-create an incident; AIOPS may correlate or suppress.
Monitoring alert breached a configured threshold. ITOM publishes; ITSM may auto-create an incident; AIOPS may correlate or suppress.

handoffs.description: An MSP customer's chat message is materialized as an MSP-PSA ticket with the channel context attached for billing and SLA.

trigger_events.description: An MSP customer's WSC message is converted to an MSP-PSA ticket. The MSP ticket carries the chat transcript and SLA clock starts.

handoffs.description: RMM monitoring alert breaches a policy threshold and creates an MSP-PSA ticket in the affected customer's queue, with telemetry snapshot, endpoint context, and SLA-aware priority. Friction is lower than the RMM-to-ITSM equivalent in unified same-vendor MSP stacks but rises in cross-vendor MSP stacks.
handoffs.notes: Same alert-to-ticket pattern as RMM→ITSM; native in unified vendor stacks, friction high in cross-vendor combinations.

trigger_events.description: Monitoring alert breached a configured threshold. ITOM publishes; ITSM may auto-create an incident; AIOPS may correlate or suppress.
Time entry approved; eligible for billing or block-hour decrement.

handoffs.description: Remote session duration flows to MSP-PSA for billable time capture.

trigger_events.description: A REMOTE-ACCESS support session has ended. ITSM ticket time captured; MSP-PSA billing engages; recording archived.

handoffs.description: Session duration should populate a billable time entry in MSP-PSA, but in cross-vendor MSP stacks technicians manually transcribe session minutes into the PSA. Failure modes: session minutes go unbilled, customer disputes arise over after-the-fact time entries, productivity reporting under-counts work.
handoffs.notes: Classic time-tracking friction in cross-vendor MSP stacks; native in unified single-vendor MSP stacks.

trigger_events.description: Fired when a MSP Time Entry is completed. Publisher domain owns the state transition; subscribers may react by creating downstream artifacts.
An MSP master service agreement has been activated. PSA can begin billing; ERP-FIN sets up recurring invoice schedule; CSM kicks off onboarding.
MSP contract paused (non-payment, dispute). SLAs paused; billing held.
Customer or RMM agent has opened a new MSP ticket.

handoffs.description: Tier-1 ticket escalates to a remote-session need; technician launches the remote-control tool against the affected endpoint. Failure modes: ticket-to-endpoint mapping is hostname-based and breaks for shifting laptop names; session recording rarely auto-links back to the ticket.
handoffs.notes: Parallel to ITSM→RMM ticket.escalated handoff.

trigger_events.description: Fired when a MSP Ticket is escalated. Publisher domain owns the state transition; subscribers may react by creating downstream artifacts.

handoffs.description: New supplier records in S2P (with DUNS, tax IDs, bank details) must propagate to SPEND-MGMT for bill-pay payee setup. Different identifier spaces (internal vendor_id, DUNS, supplier_code) create duplicate vendor records and routing errors. Classic identity-reconciliation pattern.

trigger_events.description: Fired when a Supplier is added. Publisher domain owns the state transition; subscribers may react by creating downstream artifacts.

handoffs.description: An approved pre-trip authorization with an estimated cost is handed to the spend domain as a pre-committed spend request, so the projected travel spend is visible before the charges land.

trigger_events.description: A pre-trip authorization is approved, releasing the trip for booking or confirming an out-of-policy exception.

handoffs.description: Policy changes authored in EXPENSE (per-category limits, prohibited MCCs, approver thresholds) must propagate to SPEND-MGMT real-time card-auth rules. Drift between submission-time checks and authorization-time checks leads to declined valid transactions or approved out-of-policy spend. Cross-vendor stack pattern with same logical entity.

trigger_events.description: Fired when a Expense Policy is updated. Publisher domain owns the state transition; subscribers may react by creating downstream artifacts.

handoffs.description: Policy violations feed into spend governance dashboards and exception reviews.

trigger_events.description: An expense line triggered a policy violation (over-cap, missing receipt, out-of-policy merchant). SPEND-MGMT and AUDIT capture; manager review required.

handoffs.description: Out-of-policy travel surfaces in spend governance for manager approval.

trigger_events.description: A travel booking violated travel policy. SPEND-MGMT and AUDIT capture; manager approval may be required pre-trip.

handoffs.description: Outside counsel engaged triggers accrual and engagement-letter spend tracking in Spend Management.

trigger_events.description: An outside counsel engagement has been created. Triggers spend tracking and engagement-letter generation.

handoffs.description: Cleared invoices update committed-spend actuals in SPEND-MGMT.

trigger_events.description: Three-way match (PO, receipt, invoice) succeeded. AP-AUTO releases for payment; ERP-FIN posts the liability; S2P closes the PO line.

handoffs.description: An engagement action plan transitions to completed in EMP-EXP. Subscribers in WORK-MGMT close the work_items that tracked each action item and roll up completion for reporting. Failure mode: action items may be closed in EMP-EXP without the linked work_items being closed in WORK-MGMT, leaving stale tasks.

trigger_events.description: Engagement action plan marked complete. Follow-up pulse survey scheduling possible; impact-measurement recorded.

handoffs.description: When content is flagged stale during recertification, an improvement work item is created in Work Management for remediation.

trigger_events.description: An owner (or the cadence elapsing) has flagged content as stale, requiring remediation or archival; spawns an improvement work item.

handoffs.description: Engagement action plans often tracked as work items in WORK-MGMT for execution visibility.

trigger_events.description: Engagement action plan created from survey insights. HCM and TALENT-MGMT align development and retention motions; WORK-MGMT may track tasks.

handoffs.description: A converted intake form submission spawns a work item in the task-execution module under the routed project.

trigger_events.description: A work_form_submission has been converted to a work_item in the target project. The submission record stays for audit trail; downstream work happens on the spawned work_item.

handoffs.description: Promoting a roadmap item to now/next must create the corresponding delivery work in WORK-MGMT; manual handoff here is one of the most-cited PROD↔ENG pain points.

trigger_events.description: A roadmap item has moved from later to now/next (or committed). Creates WORK-MGMT delivery scope; CSM may notify advocating customers.

handoffs.description: A product release ships in PROD-MGMT. WORK-MGMT subscribers close the work_items that tracked release-prep tasks and surface release notes against the project board.

trigger_events.description: A product release has been deployed to GA. DXP publishes release notes; CSM packages the customer communication; CRM updates entitled-features; CDP refreshes segments based on new capabilities.

handoffs.description: SPM creates work_projects + kickoff work_items for charter and resourcing.

trigger_events.description: Approved demand becomes authorized initiative or roadmap item.

handoffs.description: PSA seeds the WORK-MGMT project board with the newly-assigned resource so day-to-day task tracking can begin.
handoffs.notes: target NULL until WORK-MGMT declares consumer DMDO on `project_assignments`

trigger_events.description: A consultant or named resource is firmly assigned to a project role with a start date and percentage allocation. Triggers HCM capacity decrement, WORK-MGMT seat creation, and finance commitment recognition.

handoffs.description: Executive-level OKRs created in SPM (or in a slide deck, or an HCM perf system) need to cascade into team-level OKRs in the work-management tool. Almost universally manual: someone reads the corporate OKR and authors child OKRs in the WORK-MGMT goals module. The cascade gap is what dedicated OKR-platform vendors exist to close.
handoffs.notes: High-friction shape: probabilistic-to-deterministic. Strategic OKRs are written narratively; team OKRs need to be measurable and assigned. The translation step has no canonical engine.

trigger_events.description: An OKR is created in one OKR-mastering domain (typically SPM with strategic intent or HCM with performance-cycle intent) and needs to cascade to team-level OKRs in WORK-MGMT. The cascade is rarely automated, and the resulting gap drives a dedicated OKR-platform market.

handoffs.description: A product release is rolled back in PROD-MGMT (post-ship regression or incident). WORK-MGMT subscribers reopen the work_items that tracked the release and spawn remediation tasks. Failure mode: remediation tasks may not be scoped correctly if the rollback reason isn't propagated.

trigger_events.description: A product release has been rolled back due to defects or customer impact. CSM mobilizes for incident comms; DXP retracts the launch content.

handoffs.description: Extracted business rule routed for analyst validation and possible codification.

trigger_events.description: Business rule extracted from event-log patterns; rule catalog updates; LCAP/BPA may codify.

handoffs.description: Approved initiatives cascade into team-level work items in WORK-MGMT.

trigger_events.description: An SPM business value assessment has finalized. EPM updates the portfolio NPV; TALENT-MGMT may use for goal cascading.

handoffs.description: Webhook delivery failures create tasks for integration owners to investigate.

trigger_events.description: A webhook subscription failed delivery beyond the configured retry budget. The subscriber must investigate; iPaaS may auto-disable.

handoffs.description: Automation rules can drive OKR check-in updates or auto-progress KRs based on work_item events. Eventful (out-of-process at runtime) because automation execution decouples from the caller.

trigger_events.description: A WORK-MGMT automation rule fired and produced downstream task effects. Generic signal for cross-tool task mirroring.

handoffs.description: Committing an OKR unlocks KR-to-work_item linking and optionally auto-creates placeholder work_items per the objective's templates. Reverse direction of the rollup flow.

trigger_events.description: A team-execution OKR is committed: KRs are finalized, owners set, and downstream task-creation / KR-to-task linking may now happen. Subscribers in TASK-EXEC create placeholder work_items or link existing ones to the freshly-committed KRs.

handoffs.description: PSA task completion mirrors into the WORK-MGMT board to keep team-level views current.
handoffs.notes: target NULL until WORK-MGMT declares consumer DMDO on `project_tasks`

trigger_events.description: A delivery task on the project plan has been marked complete. WORK-MGMT mirrors the status; PSA aggregates for milestone progress and EPM consumes for delivery KPI rollup.

handoffs.description: Bottleneck findings spawn improvement tasks in WORK-MGMT.

trigger_events.description: A simulation run flagged a process bottleneck. PROD-MGMT and SPM consume for process-improvement prioritization.

handoffs.description: Once demand-signal crosses the prioritization threshold, an engineering work item / epic is created in WORK-MGMT. Many teams still do this by hand.

trigger_events.description: Upvote / weighted-demand score for a feature request crossed the configured prioritization threshold. Triggers PM review and downstream WORK-MGMT initiative consideration.

handoffs.description: When a plan line is scheduled on the marketing calendar, the delivery work is handed to work-management as tasks and projects. Payload: the work item that delivers the plan line.

trigger_events.description: A plan line has been placed on the marketing calendar and handed to execution and delivery teams.

handoffs.description: New defects materialize as work items on the engineering team's board for triage and fix.

trigger_events.description: A test execution surfaced a new defect. Triggers triage workflow in WORK-MGMT; ITSM may track if customer-impacting.

handoffs.description: Terminal completion of a work item is the strongest progress signal — drives KR closure recalculation and triggers KR-fully-met evaluations on linked objectives.

trigger_events.description: A work_item transitions to done/complete state in a WORK-MGMT platform. Used by SPM for portfolio rollup, by PSA for billable hours close-out, and by ITSM when the work_item was linked to an IT ticket.

handoffs.description: A project assignment is released in PSA (consultant rolls off or capacity is freed). WORK-MGMT subscribers may close or reassign the work_items that were owned by the released assignee. Failure mode: orphaned work_items if the release event is missed and no reassignment happens.

trigger_events.description: A resource rolls off a project (planned end reached, early release, or scope change). Returns capacity to the HCM bench, closes the WORK-MGMT seat, and may trigger SWP demand-replan.

handoffs.description: A new or updated product roadmap is published in PROD-MGMT. WORK-MGMT subscribers create work_projects or sub-projects representing the new roadmap initiatives so cross-functional teams can begin execution tracking.

trigger_events.description: A new product-roadmap version has been published. DXP updates customer-facing roadmap; CRM/CSM refresh narrative for renewal and expansion conversations.

handoffs.description: Sales closes a deal in CRM; delivery / Customer Success spin up a kickoff project in their work-management tool. Custom iPaaS automations or hand-built webhooks bridge the two; payload mapping (opportunity products to project tasks, account stakeholders to project members) is bespoke per org.
handoffs.notes: High-friction shape: cross-vendor stack with the same logical entity. Mainstream CRM platforms don't ship a canonical 'project from won opportunity' flow; every services-delivery org reinvents the bridge. Reusing existing trigger_event id 84.

trigger_events.description: Fired when a Opportunity is closed won. Publisher domain owns the state transition; subscribers may react by creating downstream artifacts.

handoffs.description: Work item status change triggers KR progress recalculation in GOALS-OKR for any objective that has linked the item to a key result. In-process FK + state read; no message moves.

trigger_events.description: Generic status transition on a work_item. Subscribers care about specific states (blocked, in_review, done) but the platform emits one event with the new status as payload. The atomic synchronization event for cross-tool work-item mirroring across work-management and ITSM platforms.

handoffs.description: WORK-MGMT creates the delivery workstream / release train for the planned release, with the scope and target date hydrated from PROD-MGMT.

trigger_events.description: A product release has been scheduled with a target date and scope. WORK-MGMT creates the delivery workstream; DXP plans the launch content.

handoffs.description: PR merges transition the linked work item to a completed state in the team's WORK-MGMT board.

trigger_events.description: A pull request has been merged to a tracked branch. Triggers CD pipeline kickoff, release-note generation, and traceability linkage.

handoffs.description: Re-prioritization cascades to project priority updates; high-touch validation.

trigger_events.description: Portfolio composition or prioritization changes; cascades to children.

handoffs.description: No-code automation creates a work item in the WORK-MGMT platform when its trigger fires.

trigger_events.description: A no-code automation fired; downstream WORK-MGMT or LCAP may pick up the action.

handoffs.description: Mining tool detects significant conformance deviation against the published model; process owner is alerted to redesign. Today usually a human handoff (ticket, email, PowerPoint review). Failure modes: deviations ignored, root cause attribution unclear, redesign cycle takes months.

trigger_events.description: PROC-MIN detects a runtime deviation from the designed process — surfaces back to BPA for model review.

handoffs.description: Value-stream bottleneck identified; the underlying process models in the repository are flagged for reengineering.

trigger_events.description: BPA's simulation or analysis identifies a bottleneck in a value stream — consumers (PROD-MGMT, etc.) re-prioritize.

handoffs.description: Process variants feed BPA conformance reviews.

trigger_events.description: A new process variant identified; conformance or improvement candidates surfaced.

handoffs.description: Capability map updated; process models grouped under the changed capabilities are flagged for review in the process repository.

trigger_events.description: BPA publishes an updated business capability map — consumers re-align coverage assessments.

handoffs.description: As-is process model published to BPA tooling for comparison against to-be design.

trigger_events.description: Discovered as-is process model published; BPA can compare against to-be; WORK-MGMT teams review.

handoffs.description: Process simulation run surfaces a bottleneck; the simulated process model in the repository is flagged for revision.

trigger_events.description: A simulation run flagged a process bottleneck. PROD-MGMT and SPM consume for process-improvement prioritization.

handoffs.description: When a data asset is deprecated in the catalog, downstream metrics that reference it should be flagged or auto-deprecated. Almost universally manual today: catalog tools surface the deprecation, but a human has to walk the metric registry to identify and deprecate dependents.
handoffs.notes: High-friction shape: lineage staleness. The catalog-side knows the asset is deprecated; the metric-side may not pick it up for weeks. The gap exists because lineage tools are immature at metric-to-asset granularity.

trigger_events.description: A previously certified metric is deprecated (with optional replacement metric reference). Triggers consumer warnings on BI dashboards and AI-agent tool-use prompts, with a grace period before retirement.

handoffs.description: MDM golden records are the authoritative source for master entities (Customer, Product, Supplier). KGP ingests them and links to ontology classes, but the data models differ: MDM is record-centric and survivorship-driven, KGP is relationship-centric and reasoning-driven. Bidirectional sync is bespoke.
handoffs.notes: High-friction shape: cross-vendor stack with the same logical entity. The 'is the MDM Customer the same as the KGP Person entity?' reconciliation problem is the canonical failure mode.

trigger_events.description: A KG entity gains a new relationship link (sameAs, partOf, derived from an inference run, or manually asserted). Triggers downstream re-reasoning, embedding-recomputation for similarity search, and notification of AI agents that hold the entity in context.

handoffs.description: New glossary term published → KGP (Knowledge Graph Platform) populates concept hierarchy and links related entities.

trigger_events.description: Business term published; semantically links to assets and ontologies.

handoffs.description: Data Catalog and Governance platforms maintain business glossaries that semantically overlap with KGP ontologies. When a glossary term is added/changed, KGP ontology should reflect (and vice-versa). Almost universally manual; very few tools bridge the two models automatically.
handoffs.notes: High-friction shape: probabilistic glossary terms to deterministic ontology concepts. Some tools bridge both sides natively; others rely on manual stewardship.

trigger_events.description: A new ontology version is published. Triggers ontology-reload in dependent KGP instances, federated SPARQL endpoint refresh, AI-agent schema-cache invalidation, and downstream consumers (DCG glossaries, MDM mappings) revalidation.

handoffs.description: External share evaluated against DLP policy for sensitive data exposure.

trigger_events.description: A no-code view is shared via public link or external user; DLP needs to validate.

handoffs.description: Policy approved → DLP activates PII masking for named users.

trigger_events.description: Access request to an asset approved by steward; IGA/DLP receive grant signal.

handoffs.description: When a user's risk score breaches threshold, Data Loss Prevention enforcement can be tightened for that user (risk-adaptive policy), narrowing what they can exfiltrate while a case proceeds.

trigger_events.description: A user's risk score crossed a configured threshold, signaling elevated insider risk and prompting alert generation.

handoffs.description: External share triggers DLP policy evaluation for sensitive data exposure.
