trigger_events.description: BI dashboard shared with external users or via public link; DLP and governance need to validate.

handoffs.description: New egress sink registers with DLP for policy enforcement on destination.

trigger_events.description: New sink (destination) connector configured; egress path registered with DLP.

handoffs.description: New domain scope informs DLP rule targeting for sensitive content within the domain.

trigger_events.description: A new data domain registered with steward and policy scope; DQ and DLP receive scope updates.

handoffs.description: Classification update fires DLP rule re-evaluation.

trigger_events.description: Sensitivity label applied to a data warehouse.

handoffs.description: Newly captured documents are scanned by DLP for sensitive content; quarantine or classification suggestions are written back.

trigger_events.description: A new document is captured into ECM. DLP scans for sensitive content; classification rules apply; downstream KMS may index a published copy.

handoffs.description: Posted messages are streamed to DLP for content inspection and policy enforcement.
handoffs.notes: target NULL until DLP is modularized

trigger_events.description: A chat message is posted. DLP scans for sensitive content; ECM may capture for retention; KMS may extract knowledge fragments.

handoffs.description: DCG publishes classification label; DLP must update enforcement policies.

trigger_events.description: Sensitivity label applied; DLP/DSPM react to enforce/audit.

handoffs.description: Classification label changes drive DLP policy recomputation (egress, sharing, retention enforcement).

trigger_events.description: An ECM classification (confidential, restricted, public, PII-laden) is applied or changed. DLP enforces matching policy; IGA realigns access entitlements.

handoffs.description: New connector registers in DSPM for scanning the source system inventory.

trigger_events.description: New source connector configured; DCG registers new data assets; DSPM may scan.

handoffs.description: Anomalous usage spike escalates to data-security posture review.

trigger_events.description: Unusual spike in query/usage of an asset; security and FinOps may inspect.

handoffs.description: DCG publishes classification; DSPM re-evaluates posture and alerts on over-privileged access.

trigger_events.description: Sensitivity label applied; DLP/DSPM react to enforce/audit.

handoffs.description: Space utilization triggers real estate re-planning.

trigger_events.description: Space occupancy metrics updated.

handoffs.description: An approaching lease critical date alerts the real-estate and facilities team to exercise or decline a renewal or option.

trigger_events.description: A lease critical date is approaching its deadline: an alert fires to the lease administrator to act on the option, renewal, or notice.

handoffs.description: Async, often delayed (technician retro logging); leaver/cancellation recall pattern on vacated spaces.

trigger_events.description: Work completed; asset history + cost captured.

handoffs.description: Agent-side has cleared inspection, financing, and appraisal contingencies; broker oversight takes the transaction into compliance review before authorizing closing.

trigger_events.description: All inspection, financing, and appraisal contingencies have been removed; transaction is ready for compliance review.

handoffs.description: Broker compliance review approved; transaction returns to agent-side for closing coordination.

trigger_events.description: Broker compliance review completed; transaction approved for closing.

handoffs.description: Broker disbursed commission; agent-side surfaces the paid status for the recipient agent.

trigger_events.description: Commission disbursed to recipient agent or cooperating brokerage.

handoffs.description: Closed sale of a rental property results in a new landlord-of-record; the new owner's property-management platform must be configured (often manual handoff via email; the buyer's PM and the seller's brokerage are different vendors).

trigger_events.description: Real estate transaction has closed (deed recorded, funds disbursed). New owner becomes the landlord-of-record; brokerage commission is earned and disbursable.

handoffs.description: Property master flows to CRE for tenant/lease planning.

trigger_events.description: Real estate property added to master inventory.

handoffs.description: Closed sale triggers commercial lease setup if multi-tenant.

trigger_events.description: Property sold; listing closed.

handoffs.description: Closed sale of a CRE asset transfers operations to the new owner's CRE platform; rent-roll, leases, and CAM history must be carried over (typically manual).

trigger_events.description: Real estate transaction has closed (deed recorded, funds disbursed). New owner becomes the landlord-of-record; brokerage commission is earned and disbursable.

handoffs.description: Realized rental income feeds multifamily-fund NOI calculations and ultimately property valuations and investor reporting.
handoffs.notes: Batched monthly; misses on residential-PM-to-investment-mgmt timing cascade to NAV-refresh delays.

trigger_events.description: Tenant rent payment has been received and reconciled; posts to per-property GL and triggers owner-distribution calculation.

handoffs.description: Sale closing triggers fund NAV and LP-reporting recalculation.

trigger_events.description: Property sold; listing closed.

handoffs.description: Property updates trigger investment-valuation recalculation.

trigger_events.description: Property attributes (address, sqft, zoning) modified.

handoffs.description: Tenant credit risk updates asset valuation models.

trigger_events.description: Tenant financial credit reviewed; risk updated.

handoffs.description: New executed lease updates rent roll and NOI for the property; flows into RE-INVEST valuation models (often via a separate investment-valuation tool file refresh, since CRE-ops and the valuation tool rarely share schema).
handoffs.notes: Multi-shape: cross-vendor-stack (CRE-ops platform on ops side, investment-valuation tool on investment side) + identifier reconciliation (suite-level rent-roll keys differ across systems). The classic 'high-friction' RE handoff.

trigger_events.description: Commercial lease has been signed by both parties; triggers rent-roll update, NOI recalculation, and CAM-allocation update.

handoffs.description: FSM work-order dispatch assigns a technician's vehicle for the day's route; FLEET-MGMT records the assignment and telematics activates against it.
handoffs.notes: Common cross-vendor stack: FSM platform + telematics platform. Identifier reconciliation on technician-to-driver and vehicle-id is the typical gap.

trigger_events.description: Vehicle has been dispatched on an assignment (FSM job, route, delivery). Triggers telematics-tracking activation against this assignment context.

handoffs.description: Critical defects flag vehicle out-of-service.

trigger_events.description: Vehicle maintenance issue logged.

handoffs.description: Risky-behavior events stream into FLEET-MGMT for driver-safety scoring and coaching-queue management.
handoffs.notes: Intra-cluster handoff (telematics to fleet workflow); typically same-vendor and low friction.

trigger_events.description: Telematics-detected risky-behavior event (harsh brake, speeding, fatigue). Feeds driver-safety scoring and coaching workflow; severe events escalate to fleet-manager review.

handoffs.description: Driver safety scores surface in performance dashboards.

trigger_events.description: Driver safety score recalculated from telemetry.

handoffs.description: Completed trips stream into fleet-utilization analytics, productive-time scoring, and fuel-trip reconciliation.
handoffs.notes: Intra-cluster low-friction when same vendor; cross-vendor still needs reliable trip-end semantics.

trigger_events.description: Vehicle trip has ended (engine off, idle threshold, or geofence exit). Triggers utilization update, fuel-trip reconciliation, and IFTA jurisdiction allocation.

handoffs.description: Service dispatch optimizes technician vehicle routing.

trigger_events.description: Work order dispatched to technician.

handoffs.description: Telemetry feed is consumed by TELEMATICS for utilization/efficiency analytics.

trigger_events.description: A machinery telemetry record (GPS/coverage/yield/engine-hours) has been captured; downstream TELEMATICS aggregates utilization, ERP-FIN allocates machine-cost, FOOD-TRACE links to operation KDE.

handoffs.description: Vehicle assignment activates real-time telematics.

trigger_events.description: Vehicle assigned to driver; telematics monitoring activated.

handoffs.description: Published prescription map is exported to machinery telematics systems for in-cab execution.

trigger_events.description: A variable-rate prescription map has been published for application; downstream TELEMATICS pushes the map to machinery and FOOD-TRACE links it to the resulting application KDE.

handoffs.description: New vehicle enrollment triggers maintenance-schedule creation.

trigger_events.description: New vehicle added to fleet.

handoffs.description: Mileage milestones trigger preventive-maintenance orders.

trigger_events.description: Vehicle mileage crossed maintenance trigger.

handoffs.description: Failed DVIR inspection defects route to FLEET-MAINT as a new vehicle work order with the defect description and severity.
handoffs.notes: Single-vendor stacks solve this in-platform; cross-vendor fails when DVIR app and maintenance system are different vendors.

trigger_events.description: DVIR found one or more defects requiring repair. Routes to FLEET-MAINT for work-order creation; severe defects ground the vehicle.

handoffs.description: Telematics-tracked mileage / engine hours / fault codes trigger PM-schedule firings that auto-generate vehicle work orders in the maintenance system.
handoffs.notes: Cross-vendor stack: telematics platform on one side, fleet-maintenance platform on the other; identifier reconciliation on vehicle id is the common pain point.

trigger_events.description: PM trigger has fired (mileage, engine hours, calendar, or DTC code). Triggers work-order auto-generation and shop scheduling.

handoffs.description: When an agency wins new business in CRM, AGENCY-MGMT needs to spin up an agency_job with the client, scope, billing terms, and a placeholder team. The handoff translates sales-side opportunity attributes (forecast value, close date) into delivery-side job attributes (scope, brief, rate plan).
handoffs.notes: Friction shape: scope translation — sales-stage scope rarely matches the level of detail an agency_job needs (deliverable list, rate card, retainer linkage). Often requires a kick-off meeting to finalize.

trigger_events.description: An agency new-business opportunity reaches Closed Won in CRM, triggering downstream job spin-up in AGENCY-MGMT.

handoffs.description: Signed SOW or MSA from CLM seeds billing rules, rate card, scope envelope, and SLA terms onto the agency_job. Subsequent change orders also flow this way.
handoffs.notes: Friction shape: identifier reconciliation — CLM SOW ID needs to map to the agency_job ID, and signing-party data needs to match the client record.

trigger_events.description: Fired when a Contract is signed. Publisher domain owns the state transition; subscribers may react by creating downstream artifacts.

handoffs.description: Media-outlet or freelancer invoice arrives via S2P and needs three-way match against the originating insertion_order (quantity, rate, make-good provisions) before booking against the job for cost-plus billing.
handoffs.notes: Friction shape: cross-vendor stack — media-outlet invoicing is notoriously inconsistent (rate variances, make-good adjustments, late arrivals). Manual reconciliation rate often >20%.

trigger_events.description: Media-outlet or freelancer invoice arrives via S2P; matched against the originating insertion_order with quantity and rate reconciliation.

handoffs.description: Agency staff member terminated in HCM; AGENCY-MGMT must reassign open job tasks, freeze the employee's time entry capability (but preserve historical entries for billing), and trigger access removal for project tooling.
handoffs.notes:
Friction shape: leaver/cancellation recall — termination event is harder to act on than onboarding; open tasks and in-flight deliverables need explicit reassignment, and time-entry locking has to coexist with historical-record preservation.

target_domain_module_id NULL until AGENCY-MGMT is modularized (Phase-M gap on target domain; SKILL.md authoring rule).

trigger_events.description: Fired when a Employee is terminated. Publisher domain owns the state transition; subscribers may react by creating downstream artifacts.

handoffs.description: Farm-side harvest event seeds the upstream traceability lot at the processor or grower-shipper; lot-code reconciliation between FMIS field-keyed records and FOOD-TRACE lot-keyed records is the integration burden.
handoffs.notes: Cross-vendor stack with same logical entity: FMIS on the production side vs FOOD-TRACE on the processor side; identifier reconciliation is largely manual or hand-mapped today.

trigger_events.description: A field harvest event has been recorded with yield, harvest date, and field reference; downstream creates the upstream traceability lot AND realizes available-share inventory for direct-sales planning.

handoffs.description: When an animal or mob is sold or sent to slaughter, the sale and identity records hand off to food traceability so the carcass lot can be tied back to the animal's on-farm provenance and movement history.

trigger_events.description: An animal or mob has been sold or sent to slaughter; the on-farm lifecycle closes and the carcass enters the downstream traceability chain.

handoffs.description: CCP deviation flags affected lots in FOOD-TRACE for hold and downstream tracing.

trigger_events.description: A CCP measurement has deviated from the critical limit (temp/pH/time/aw); downstream MFG-OPS quarantines the production lot, FOOD-TRACE flags affected lots, and GRC logs the deviation for reporting.

handoffs.description: A severity-escalated food-safety incident creates a recall-execution record in FOOD-TRACE; recall-decision threshold is judgment-heavy and recall-execution is a regulator-prescribed workflow.
handoffs.notes: Multi-shape: probabilistic-to-deterministic (incident severity scoring → recall yes/no) + cross-vendor stack (FSQM vs FOOD-TRACE). The escalation point is the highest-stakes manual judgment in the food-safety lifecycle.

trigger_events.description: A food-safety incident has been escalated to recall status; downstream creates the recall execution record and notifies regulators.

handoffs.description: Field boundary update propagates lot-origin geometry to FOOD-TRACE.

trigger_events.description: A field boundary/geometry has been updated; downstream FOOD-TRACE updates lot-to-field linkage, TELEMATICS recomputes geofences, and ERP-FIN updates land-cost allocation.

handoffs.description: Feed-ration change links ingredient lots to milk lots for downstream traceability.

trigger_events.description: A feed ration formulation has been changed for a group; downstream ERP-FIN updates feed-cost-per-liter and FOOD-TRACE links ingredient lots for traceability.

handoffs.description: Application records (especially restricted-use pesticides) become KDE evidence for residue-traceback investigations and provenance attestation.

trigger_events.description: A chemical / fertilizer application pass has been recorded with product, rate, applicator, and weather conditions; downstream creates a KDE entry for traceability and feeds organic / certification-program evidence.

handoffs.description: Completed produced unit feeds FOOD-TRACE as a CTE/KDE entry for the produced lot.

trigger_events.description: A unit has been completed on the line with serial/batch identity; downstream FOOD-TRACE captures the KDE/CTE record and ERP-FIN updates inventory.

handoffs.description: Ready butcher order finalizes lot/cut linkage in FOOD-TRACE for source-animal traceability.

trigger_events.description: A butcher order is cut, packed and ready for pickup/delivery; downstream CRM notifies the customer and FOOD-TRACE finalizes the lot/cut traceability record.

handoffs.description: When a treatment is recorded, its withholding period and the animals it applies to hand off to food traceability so an animal still inside a withholding window is blocked from entering the food chain.

trigger_events.description: A treatment or medicine has been administered, opening a withholding period that gates sale and slaughter eligibility until it clears.

handoffs.description: Each milking aggregates into bulk-tank lots that FOOD-TRACE captures as upstream traceability records.

trigger_events.description: A milking event has been completed for a cow/parlor-session with volume and composition; downstream FOOD-TRACE rolls into bulk-tank lots and ERP-FIN aggregates daily yield.

handoffs.description: Dairy-farm milk dispatch seeds the downstream traceability lot at the processor; tank-truck commingling and farm-source apportionment is complex.
handoffs.notes: Cross-vendor stack: dairy farm-management systems and processor's traceability platform rarely share schema; commingled tanks across multiple farms make per-farm-source attribution non-trivial.

trigger_events.description: A bulk milk shipment has left the farm with volume, hauler, and quality-grade attestation; downstream creates a traceability lot at the processor.

handoffs.description: Positive environmental sample drives FOOD-TRACE evaluation of which lots to hold.

handoffs.description: An activated value stream begins flowing measured data into the flow-metrics and insights module.

trigger_events.description: A delivery value stream has been modeled and activated for flow measurement.

handoffs.description: A confirmed booking prompts guide and resource scheduling to assign staff and equipment to the departure.

trigger_events.description: A booking is confirmed (payment captured or hold accepted). Drives guide assignment, waiver dispatch, manifest update, and channel availability sync.

handoffs.description: When all participants have signed, the booking is marked ready for the departure.

trigger_events.description: A participant signs their liability waiver. Marks the participant ready and attaches the signed release to the booking.

handoffs.description: A confirmed booking reduces remaining capacity and syncs updated availability out to distribution channels.

trigger_events.description: A booking is confirmed (payment captured or hold accepted). Drives guide assignment, waiver dispatch, manifest update, and channel availability sync.

handoffs.description: A completed departure releases its assigned guides and equipment back to the scheduling pool.

trigger_events.description: A departure is completed. Closes out its bookings, releases resources, and triggers review requests.

handoffs.description: A confirmed guide assignment updates the departure manifest the core module presents to staff.

trigger_events.description: A guide confirms assignment to a departure. Updates the departure manifest and notifies the customer.

handoffs.description: A confirmed booking generates pending waivers for each participant to sign before the activity.

trigger_events.description: A booking is confirmed (payment captured or hold accepted). Drives guide assignment, waiver dispatch, manifest update, and channel availability sync.

domainRoles.description: Front-line sales leader who inspects pipeline by deal risk, runs forecast roll-ups, and coaches reps on recorded calls.
RevOps analyst who tunes deal-scoring and forecasting models, monitors forecast accuracy, and curates activity-attribution rules.
Quota-carrying rep whose activities are auto-captured, who submits a periodic forecast, and who acts on deal warnings and coaching.
Enablement coach who reviews recorded calls against the playbook and runs structured coaching sessions.
Owns the requisition-to-offer pipeline for assigned reqs: sources, screens, schedules, drafts and sends offers, drives candidates to hire.
Builds and works talent pools and the candidate CRM; generates qualified pipeline ahead of open reqs.
Owns interview logistics and offer / pre-employee paperwork; schedules panels and keeps the process moving.
Accountable for the recruiting function's output: approves reqs and offers, owns pipeline health and vendor relationships.
The role owning the open position. Cross-functional (sits in the hiring department, not Recruiting): defines the req, interviews, decides the hire, approves the offer.
Owns hiring-compliance surfaces: background-check adjudication, FCRA / adverse-action, EEO / OFCCP, and candidate data-subject requests.
PMO / BizOps lead who owns cross-team programs, triages intake, and rolls up OKR progress from work items.
Individual contributor who executes assigned work items, posts updates, and submits cross-team requests through intake.
Marketing operator who runs campaign projects with creative review and routes creative requests through intake queues.
Cross-functional objective owner who commits and scores OKRs and links key results to executing work items.

IT Operations persona that runs day-to-day SaaS administration: discovering and triaging applications, managing integrations and owners, optimizing license usage and reclamation, and operating automation workflows and self-service requests.

Procurement persona that owns the commercial SaaS lifecycle: renewal pipeline, vendor negotiations, spend allocation, and vendor risk attestation, with read access to discovery and usage data that informs renewal decisions.

IT Asset Management persona that governs the SaaS portfolio end to end across discovery, optimization, renewal, and automation; the cross-module owner accountable for portfolio cost, compliance, and lifecycle.
Owns the end-to-end contingent-workforce program: requisition intake, supplier distribution, rate-card governance, and the time-to-invoice flow. Spans worker sourcing and time-and-invoicing.
Governs the staffing-supplier panel and the rate cards: onboards and activates suppliers, approves rate cards by role and region, and monitors supplier performance against billed invoices.
Coordinates day-to-day contingent-labor operations: shepherds worker assignments and tenure tracking in sourcing, and chases timesheet approvals and invoice matching in time-and-invoicing.

Owns day-to-day operation of the learning platform: maintains the course catalog, manages enrollments and learning paths, configures automation and audiences, and administers credentials and continuing education.
Authors and versions courses, lessons, content assets, and assessments; publishes new training and retires outdated material across self-paced and instructor-led delivery.
Delivers instructor-led and virtual instructor-led sessions: runs scheduled offerings, records attendance, grades assessments, and supports learners through completion and certification.

Runs regulatory and policy training programs end to end: schedules compliance campaigns, tracks assignment completion, assembles training evidence, manages recertification, and produces regulator filings.
Cross-functional people leader who assigns and nudges direct reports through required and developmental learning, monitors completion and certification status, and follows up on overdue training.

Owns client engagements end to end: scopes the project, structures tasks and milestones, requests staffing, and drives delivery to completion. Accountable for on-time, on-scope delivery and for the project's billing readiness.

Owns the staffing and capacity workflow: matches skilled people to project demand, plans and commits resource allocations, confirms and releases assignments, and watches utilization and skill gaps across the billable workforce.

The billable practitioner who executes assigned project tasks and logs time and expenses against the engagements they work. Drives tasks to completion and submits clean actuals for approval and billing.

Owns project billing and revenue: manages budgets and rate cards, invoices reached milestones and approved time, and recognizes project revenue. Accountable for accurate, auditable project financials feeding the general ledger.

Accountable for the contract lifecycle end to end: owns the repository, signs off on approvals and executions, drives obligation tracking and renewals, and keeps authoring and negotiation moving across the team.
Runs the day-to-day contract workflow: assembles drafts from approved templates, shepherds signature envelopes, tracks obligations to closure, and processes renewals ahead of expiry.
Reviews and approves contract language, clause and template content, and redlines counterparty terms during negotiation. The legal gate on what the organization is willing to sign.
Bridges sourcing and contracting: turns awarded sourcing outcomes into draft agreements, consults on supplier terms during negotiation, and reads the repository for active supplier commitments.
Site Reliability Engineer
NOC / Incident Analyst
IT Operations Manager
AIOps ML Engineer
Data Center Manager
Critical Facilities Engineer
Capacity Planner
Data Center Technician
Contact Center Agent
Contact Center Supervisor
Quality Analyst
Contact Center Operations Manager
Routing and IVR Flow Administrator
Vulnerability Analyst
Vulnerability Management Program Manager
Remediation Owner
Application Remediation Engineer
Risk and Compliance Approver

Administers the HCM system of record: configures and maintains worker data, the org-unit structure, the job and position catalog, and the lifecycle workflow configuration. Holds admin authority across all HCM modules.

Executes the day-to-day worker lifecycle: processes hires into active workers, transfers and other employment events, leaves of absence, contract changes, and terminations. The transactional HR operator.
Advises managers on org changes, workforce moves, and employee relations. Accountable for sensitive lifecycle changes in their business unit and consulted on position and reorganization decisions.
Models the organization: authors and publishes job profiles, defines and approves positions against budgeted headcount, and maintains the org-unit hierarchy through reorganizations.

Owns an assigned product area end to end: triages feedback and feature requests in discovery, prioritizes and accepts work onto the roadmap, and shepherds features, releases, and beta programs from planning through ship.

Accountable for the product function's output: approves the published roadmap, owns product-line strategy and lifecycle transitions, and signs off prioritization and launch decisions across the portfolio.
Runs product operations: keeps roadmap and backlog hygiene, instruments and reports adoption and quality metrics, and coordinates release and beta logistics across teams.
Leads delivery of prioritized product work: takes accepted features through in-delivery and release, reports shipped and rolled-back states, and feeds feasibility input back into discovery.
Owns the marketing automation platform: configures campaigns, journeys, lead scoring, and forms, and keeps the program running across modules.
Plans and runs marketing campaigns and nurture journeys end to end, from authoring through launch and follow-up.
Frontline HR service agent: picks up employee cases from the portal queue, triages and classifies them, works them to resolution, and attaches knowledge. Reopens closed cases when something changes.

Accountable for HR service delivery output: owns the case queue, SLAs, routing rules, and the approval gate. Oversees workload, aging, and escalations across the case workflow and the employee portal.
Owns the HR knowledge base: curates and publishes articles, organizes them by case category, and promotes resolved cases into reusable knowledge to deflect future requests.
Owns the intranet governance program across all connected sources: sets policy, oversees recertification, and is accountable for content currency and accountability coverage.
Accountable owner for specific pieces of intranet content; responds to recertification attestations and remediates or archives stale content.
Connects and maintains intranet sources, runs crawls and scans, and keeps the inventory and connectors healthy.
Day-to-day governance operator: authors and publishes glossary terms, proposes and approves data classifications, manages stewardship assignments, and certifies assets within a data domain.
Accountable owner of a set of data assets and data products: grants and revokes certifications, signs off access policies, and is accountable for the asset's fitness for production use.
Operates the catalog platform itself: configures and runs metadata crawlers, manages lineage capture, maintains data domains, and curates the data-product marketplace surface.
Cross-functional governance authority spanning Data Engineering and GRC: sets classification and access policy, signs off enterprise data policies, and owns regulatory mapping of the data estate.
Analyst or data-product consumer who discovers assets in the catalog, reads glossary and lineage to build trust, and requests access to governed data products through policy.
Builds and publishes the product catalog, runs the storefront, and launches coupons and promotions. Reads order activity to see what is selling and adjust merchandising.
Runs the order-to-cash flow end to end: captures carts, completes checkouts and payments, creates orders, and drives them through fulfillment and shipping. Cross-functional operations persona.
Picks, packs, and ships paid orders and manages shipments and returns. Reads order detail to fulfill against the right line items.
Owns the enterprise process architecture: maintains capability maps, governs the process model repository, and aligns value streams to strategy.
Models and analyzes business processes and value streams, runs simulations, and prepares models for review and publication.
Accountable for one or more published business processes: approves publication, sponsors reengineering, and owns process outcomes. Cross-functional persona.

Owns the corporate travel program: sets and maintains travel policy, configures the approval workflow, monitors program spend and supplier performance, and is accountable for duty-of-care readiness across the organization.
Books and manages travel on behalf of one or more travelers: shops policy-aware fares, holds and tickets reservations, builds and amends itineraries, and reapplies unused-ticket credits.

Cross-functional self-service traveler: self-books within policy, maintains their own traveler profile, submits pre-trip approval requests, views and changes their own itinerary, and acknowledges duty-of-care alerts affecting them.
Owns the end-to-end marketing planning and budget process: builds and approves plans, sets budgets, oversees allocation and spend-to-plan reconciliation, and reports plan-level performance.
Authors marketing plans and plan lines, maintains the marketing calendar, and works with budget owners to align plan lines to allocated budget.

Cross-functional owner of marketing budget governance: approves budgets and allocations, monitors spend against plan, and reconciles committed and actual spend. Often sits in or partners with Finance.

Owns the site safety program: incident investigation, hazard and risk assessment, corrective actions, inspections, and required training. Accountable for closing incidents and verifying corrective actions.
Plans and runs exposure monitoring and industrial-hygiene sampling, manages occupational-health surveillance, and governs the chemical inventory and safety data sheets.
Owns environmental permits, conditions, and limits, emissions and release records, and ISO 14001 conformance; accountable for permit renewals and environmental reporting.
Cross-functional site leader accountable for the whole EHS program at an establishment, spanning safety, occupational health, environmental compliance, and audit readiness.
Prepares lease accounting: classifies leases, maintains right-of-use and liability schedules, records modifications and remeasurements, and generates the journal entries for the general ledger.
Maintains the lease record system: agreements and documents, critical dates and alerts, renewals and terminations, and the payment terms that feed lease accounting.
Owns lease-accounting policy and the close: approves classifications and modifications, reviews and files disclosures, and signs off on the lease subledger for financial reporting.
Runs the whole grazing operation: oversees herd performance, grazing plans, sales, and compliance across all properties and mobs.
Manages the animals and mobs day to day: records, weights, breeding, treatments, and movements in the yard and paddock.
Plans and executes pasture rotations: allocates paddocks, sets rest periods, and matches stocking rate to carrying capacity, moving mobs accordingly.
Owns the paid social estate: campaign strategy, budget allocation across platforms, and overall performance against targets. Accountable for spend and results.
Operates day-to-day optimization: bid and budget tuning, audience iteration, pacing, and responding to threshold breaches across ad sets.
Owns ad creative: concepts and variants, dynamic creative optimization rules, and the creative approval workflow that feeds live campaigns.
Triages insider-risk alerts, tunes detection indicators, and drives day-to-day monitoring of user risk across the workforce.
Investigates escalated insider-risk cases end to end: builds the activity timeline, performs file-lineage forensics, collects evidence, and packages it for HR and Legal.
Owns the insider risk program: approves case dispositions, governs HR/Legal escalation, and oversees exit-risk monitoring policy.

Designs and deploys executable process definitions and decision tables, owns versioning and breaking-change governance, and decides the orchestration topology across the engine and the case and decision layer.
Runs the live engine: monitors running instances, triages and resolves incidents, suspends or terminates stuck instances, and keeps throughput healthy across the execution and case modules.
Works the human side of orchestrated processes: claims and completes human tasks, advances case files with ad-hoc activities and milestones, and escalates when work stalls.
Configures channels, audiences, checklist templates, and learning modules, and authors and schedules company-wide frontline broadcasts and recognition programs.

Store, plant, or field manager who cascades broadcasts to their team, assigns and verifies tasks, approves shift swaps, and recognizes workers. Cross-functional: reports into store or plant operations, not internal comms.

Deskless worker who reads and acknowledges broadcasts, completes and submits tasks and checklists, requests and claims shift swaps, finishes microlearning, and sends and receives recognition from a mobile or shared device.

Owns the employee advocacy program end to end: enrolls advocates, sets topics and goals, runs campaigns, oversees gamification and rewards, and reports reach and pipeline impact to marketing leadership.
Sources, writes, and approves shareable content and suggested share copy, organizes it into topic streams, and keeps the advocate feed and newsletters fresh and on-brand.
An enrolled employee who reshares curated content to their personal social networks, earns points and recognition, and represents the employer brand to their own audience.
Runs the short-term rental operation end to end: listings, bookings, guest experience, turnovers, and owner reporting.
Owns listing distribution and nightly pricing: channel connections, rate plans, and dynamic-pricing rules.
Handles guest communication and bookings and coordinates turnovers so each guest has a smooth stay.
Schedules and verifies housekeeping and turnover work against the booking calendar.
Produces owner statements and payouts and handles lodging-tax filing and permit compliance.
Runs the marina end to end: oversees slip inventory and assignment, reservations, the boatyard, billing, and the fuel dock.
Assigns slips, handles transient arrivals and departures, and keeps the dock and assignment board current.
Handles reservations, boater and vessel records, document collection, and front-desk billing inquiries.
Runs the boatyard: estimates and work orders, haul-out and launch scheduling, and pump-out logging.
Owns contracts, recurring and metered billing, invoicing, and fuel and store reconciliation.
Owns the operator's booking operation: configures products, departures, and rates, oversees bookings, refunds, guide scheduling, and waiver compliance, and manages distribution.
Front-line staff who take and amend bookings over the phone, at the counter, and online, collect payments, and ensure each guest has signed a waiver.
Field staff assigned to departures: confirm availability, review the manifest and participant requirements, check out equipment, and run the trip.
Manages reseller and online-travel-agency relationships, maps products to channels, sets commission terms, and keeps channel availability in sync with the operator calendar.

businessFunctions.description: Function responsible for the full worker lifecycle: hiring, paying, developing, supporting, and offboarding the workforce. Owns HRIS-equivalent domains and partners with Finance on workforce cost.
Function responsible for the books, treasury, planning, and procurement of the business.
Function responsible for contracts, regulatory compliance, intellectual property, and dispute management.
Sub-function inside Human Resources that runs corporate learning, compliance training, and skills development.
Sub-function inside Finance that runs invoice processing, three-way match, and supplier payment.
Sub-function inside Finance that runs cash, bank-account, FX, and short-term liquidity management.
Pipeline ownership, account management, quota-carrying revenue generation, and sales operations support across direct and channel motions.
Brand, demand generation, content production, internal and external communications, customer marketing, and martech operations.
Post-sale account health, expansion, retention, customer education, and onboarding for accounts after the initial sale.
Product strategy, discovery, prioritization, roadmap ownership, and release coordination for software and physical products.
Application development, platform engineering, site reliability, and quality engineering for the products and internal systems the company builds.
Infrastructure, end-user computing, service desk, and corporate IT delivery for employee-facing technology.
InfoSec policy, security operations, identity and access management, vulnerability management, and incident response.
Data engineering, business intelligence, analytics delivery, and AI/ML platform operations across the enterprise.
Supply chain planning, manufacturing, warehouse operations, logistics, and field service for physical goods movement and production.
Enterprise risk, internal audit, compliance operations, privacy office, and policy management.
CEO office, corporate strategy, business development, mergers and acquisitions, and corporate communications.
Workplace operations, real estate portfolio, environmental health and safety, and physical security premises.
Cross-functional operations: revenue operations, business operations, process improvement, and shared services not specific to any single function.
Industry research and development outside software engineering: pharmaceutical, chemical, materials, hardware, and applied R&D.
Sustainability reporting, climate accounting, ESG disclosures, and environmental and social programs.
Talent acquisition, sourcing, candidate screening, interview coordination, offer management.
Payroll calculation, gross-to-net, statutory filing, garnishments, pay distribution, payroll compliance.
Reactive and proactive customer support: contact center, case management, and customer-side field service.
Case management for employee concerns, investigations, performance management policy administration, employee engagement programs.
General ledger, period close, consolidation, statutory reporting, financial controls.
Direct and indirect tax compliance, transfer pricing, tax provision, statutory tax filing.
Customer billing, collections, cash application, credit management, AR aging.
Internal audit planning and execution, control testing, audit findings and remediation tracking.
Demand planning, supply planning, sales and operations planning, inventory optimization.
Production scheduling, shop-floor execution, quality, MES integration, OEE management.
Inbound receiving, putaway, pick/pack/ship, inventory accuracy, WMS execution.
Transportation management, freight, last-mile, customs, route optimization.
Internal field service for company-owned assets, plant maintenance, EH&S inspections.
Quota and territory design, forecasting cadence, deal desk, sales analytics, sales technology administration.
Indirect sales through partners, channel program management, partner enablement, channel incentives.
Inbound and outbound marketing campaigns, lead generation, conversion programs, marketing-sourced pipeline.
Brand identity, creative production, design systems, brand voice, digital asset management.
PR, analyst relations, customer marketing communications, and internal-facing corporate communications when housed under Marketing.
Employee-facing IT support: incident, request, knowledge management, walk-up and virtual agent service.
Endpoint management, productivity tooling, unified endpoint management, mobile, identity provisioning at the device level.
Internal developer platform, CI/CD, golden paths, internal tooling, build and release engineering.
Production operations, on-call, observability, SLO ownership, incident response for the company's own services.
Test strategy, test automation, performance testing, quality gates in delivery pipelines.
Identity lifecycle, access provisioning, joiner-mover-leaver, privileged access, identity governance.
Threat detection, alert triage, security incident response, threat intelligence, vulnerability remediation coordination.
Data pipelines, lakehouse, data integration, master data management, data catalog operations.
BI tooling, dashboarding, self-service analytics, reporting standards, analytics delivery.
ML platform, model lifecycle, AI use-case delivery, model governance, AI ethics review.
Raw materials, components, production inputs, supplier quality for goods that enter the product.
Inbound and outbound contact handling, agent workforce management, ACD/IVR operations, omnichannel routing.
Customer-side field service: on-site repair, install, maintenance dispatch, technician scheduling.
Regulatory compliance program execution, policy management, control testing, evidence collection, regulator reporting.
Shift scheduling, time and attendance, labor forecasting, frontline workforce planning.
Budgeting, forecasting, scenario planning, driver-based modeling, management reporting.
Servers, network, cloud, data center, integration platform, infrastructure-level platform engineering.
Services, software, SaaS, and indirect-spend categories. Owns SaaS-spend rationalization, supplier qualification for non-production goods.
Privacy program management, DSR fulfillment, privacy impact assessments, data subject rights operations, cross-border data flow governance.
Contract authoring, redlining, approval routing, signature, repository, obligation tracking. The operational side of legal contract management.
Patents, trademarks, trade secrets, IP licensing, IP litigation support.
Sub-function inside Finance (or independent in some orgs) that runs sourcing, supplier management, and purchase orders.
HR shared-services delivery: case management, employee self-service, knowledge, tier-1/tier-2 case escalation. The service-desk pattern applied to HR.
Performance management, succession planning, calibration, talent reviews, career development, internal mobility.
Salary planning, incentive programs, equity administration, pay equity, compensation benchmarking. The Total Rewards function minus benefits.
Engagement surveys, pulse listening, employee journey orchestration, EX programs, recognition. Cross-cuts internal comms but anchored in HR.
HR data and analytics function: workforce metrics, attrition prediction, DEI analytics, manager dashboards, predictive people insights.
First-day-through-90-day onboarding: pre-boarding paperwork, provisioning orchestration, manager and buddy programs, ramp tracking.
FinOps practice: cloud cost transparency, allocation, optimization, commitment management. Distinct from general FP&A — owns the cloud-spend lifecycle.
Hardware, software, SaaS asset lifecycle, license compliance, asset financial management. Distinct from CMDB (configuration) and from procurement (sourcing).

Front-office investment activities: deal sourcing, due diligence, portfolio construction, and fund management. Distinct from corporate Finance (CFO-side); applies to GP-side teams at VC/PE firms and to in-house investment teams at corporates.
Cross-functional operations discipline consolidating sales, marketing, and customer-success operations around revenue process, forecasting, and go-to-market data.
Health, retirement, equity, voluntary benefits enrollment, life-event handling, carrier connectivity.
Strategic workforce planning, headcount planning, scenario modeling for the workforce, plan-to-execution handoff with FP&A.

processes.process_name: Manage Enterprise Risk, Compliance, Remediation, and Resiliency
processes.description: Ensuring that an organization effectively manages its risk. Process groups are aligned with traditional risk management activities.

processes.process_name: Leverage and enhance IT for KM approaches
processes.description: Using existing technologies to improve organization's knowledge management processes. Research available third-party offerings. Develop proprietary solutions. Employ knowledge engineers, data scientists and other relevant personnel.

Identifying and implementing content management methodologies to effectively store, deliver, and facilitate access to enterprise content. Core methodologies may include prioritization of critical or high-value content, findability to ensure ease of locating relevant content, content lifecycle management, standardization of content creation, review and access, collaboration, and technology integration.

Performing activities by an organization that are fundamental to the successful operation of the organization, even across functions in a business. Capabilities defined in the PCF include business process management; portfolio, program, and project management; quality management; change management; benchmarking; environmental health and safety management; and knowledge management.

Managing interactions with current customers after the delivery of products and services. This includes developing and planning customer service practices with a focus on handling inquiries after sales, feedback, warranties, recalls, and other related processes.

Offering services to customers. This is the act of providing service delivery as a core business practice and covers identifying strategies for performing service delivery, managing resources, and delivering services to the customer.
Understanding the demands on resources and creating a plan to enable the delivery of services via those resources.

processes.process_name: Develop content management training and communication plans
processes.description: Developing training, change and communication plans to support the organization's content management practices. Define target audiences, required competencies, learning objectives, and delivery methods to ensure consistent understanding and adoption of content standards, tools, and workflows. Create communication strategies to promote awareness of content governance, reinforce expectations, and inform stakeholders of process updates, system changes, and best practices. Coordinate with internal partners to design training materials, schedule learning sessions, and disseminate communications that enable effective and compliant content creation, storage, use, and lifecycle management. Monitor participation, evaluate effectiveness, and continuously improve based on feedback and evolving organizational needs.

Overseeing key back-office processes for organizations. This category includes process groups related to planning and management accounting, revenue accounting, general accounting and reporting, fixed-asset project accounting, payroll, accounts payable and expense reimbursements, treasury operations, internal controls, tax management, international funds/consolidation, and global trade services.

Fostering external relationships with stakeholders of the entity, including investors, government and industry, the board of directors, and the general public. This is not related to customer management.

Managing process groups relevant to the business of information technology within an organization. The process groups include "Develop and manage IT customer relationships", "Develop and manage IT business strategy", " Develop and manage IT resilience and risk", " Manage information", " Develop and manage services/solutions", "Deploy services/solutions", and " Create and manage support services/solutions".

Delivering processes traditionally defined as "human resources". Process groups include those related to developing and maintaining workforce strategy, recruiting employees, developing and counseling employees, managing employee relations, rewarding and retaining employees, redeploying and retiring employees, managing employee information, and managing employee communications.
Relating to the design, construction, acquisition, and management of both productive and non-productive assets.

Creating specific plans to market offerings to customers. This process group includes processes for making budgets, identifying and developing media, pricing products and services, managing packaging, managing marketing content and promotional activities, tracking and responding to customer insight and monitoring measures established within "develop marketing strategy". Additionally, in this process group, organizations take action on plans made in earlier processes. Here, marketing and customers are managed and measured along with any supporting materials.

Charting a strategic course for marketing products/services. This will include defining the value proposition, creating a mechanism for pricing, and determining the right mix of marketing channels. Create a specific positioning and branding for the organization's offerings. Enlist marketing head to lead, with inputs from the business development and sales functions.

processes.process_name: Establish service delivery governance and strategies
processes.description: Creating rules and regulations for service delivery to the customer. Establish a system to manage performance, delivery, and direction of service delivery. Engage with the customer for satisfaction feedback. Define goals, policies, processes, and workplace layout and infrastructure as a part of the service delivery strategy.

Creating a plan for procuring materials and services. Develop strategies for sourcing materials and services. Choose the most appropriate suppliers, and develop contracts with them. Order the materials and services as per the requirements. Manage relationships with suppliers.

Processing and delivering the finished goods manufactured by the organization. Schedule the production of products. Execute the product production activities. Perform tests to oversee and ensure quality of production. Maintain records of the production process. Track lots.

Conducting reviews of content to evaluate compliance with defined standards, controls, and retention requirements. Includes auditing for semantic accuracy, metadata completeness, and AI-readiness. Consider leveraging all forms of new and evolving technology such as artificial intelligence (AI).

Enhancing and adapting content to support new or different audiences, formats, channels, or contexts while preserving core meaning and intent of the original content. This includes leveraging all forms of new and evolving technology such as artificial intelligence (AI).

processes.process_name: Manage and Operate Service Delivery System
processes.description: Managing and operating the systems, resources, and processes used to deliver services to customers, including planning, startup, ongoing operations, and service assurance.
Developing new products/services from scratch, including all activities associated with the design, prototyping, evaluation, and market testing of these planned offerings.

Making sense of the market and customers to identify the right opportunities to be capitalized, given the organization's competencies. Discern trends and shift in the market and customers. Identify the right market opportunities that fit closely with the organization's capabilities and strategy by gathering intelligence on various attributes of different market/customer segments.

processes.process_name: Plan for and align supply chain resources
processes.description: Creating strategies for production and materials. Handle the demand for the products of the organization. Develop plans for handling materials. Develop and administer the schedule for master production. Plan for distribution requirements and its constraints by reviewing and assessing distribution policies and performance and by establishing quality standards and procedures.

Administering and overseeing all activities related to logistics and warehousing. Outline and establish a strategy for the logistics function. Plan and administer the flow of inbound materials. Administer the operational activities of warehousing and outbound transportation. Manage reverse logistics including returns and exchanges.

Improving an organization's ability to compare its performance internally or externally, and maintaining benchmarking relationships with other organizations. Train staff in benchmarking. Develop technological solutions or other materials to aid benchmarking efforts. Consult with external entities to gain knowledge or tools to help benchmark.
Designing key measures that analyze and interpret how effectively the business is achieving its objectives.

Developing concrete plans for guiding and providing support to the sales function. Chart a road map for the sales function, including an analysis of historical sales data to create forecasts for anticipated sales, forming sales targets, forging partnerships with other economic agents to boost sales, devising a budget for this function, and determining metrics to measure customer management activities as well as progress in achieving sales targets.

Assisting general management in developing, maintaining, and improving employee relationships. This is accomplished through communication, performance management, processing grievances, and/or dispute. Interpret and convey organizational policies.

Creating frameworks for rewarding and recognizing employees with the objective of retaining them. Create and manage programs for provision of rewards, recognition, and motivation. Manage and administer the benefits for employees. Help assist and retain employees. Administer payroll to employees.

processes.process_name: Manage employee onboarding, training, and development
processes.description: Assisting employees in developing their capabilities, and providing them counseling services. Handle the orientation and deployment of the employees. Administer the performance of employees. Administer the development and enhancement of the employees. Provide training and development programs for employees.

Managing employee mobility and retirement. Manage the process of employee promotion and demotion. Administer separation, retirement, and leaves of absence. Outplace employees. Deploy personnel. Relocate employees in order to manage assignments.

Managing the employee reporting processes, employee inquiry process, employee information and data, and the HR information systems. Create and administer the employee metrics. Develop and handle the time and attendance systems. Refurbish the indicators for employee retention and motivation.

Charting a strategic course for business units in order to leverage opportunities, sidestep hurdles, and create synergies among each other. Create strategic road maps for the organization's units--in light of their individual resources and requirements, as well as their relationships with other business units--to achieve organizational goals.
Creating an effective plan that initiates and promotes communication and engagement among the employees and between employees and management.

Implementing final steps to complete service delivery to the customer. Evaluate success through project review, complete finance activities, and confirm delivery. Release resources and manage completion by harvesting knowledge and systems by archiving records.

Identifying, investigating, and processes warranty claims. This process includes: receipt and validation of a warranty claim; definition and diagnosis /root cause analysis of an issue and recommendation for corrective action; the determination of responsibility for settlement of the claim; the transaction being approved or denied; and the originator being notified and payment authorized. In the case of a recurring event, further investigation (definition and diagnosis or root cause analysis) is performed, and a recommendation for corrective action is made and implemented in production/design. It ends when the claim is closed.

processes.process_name: Plan and manage customer service contacts
processes.description: Planning and administering workforce operations for customer service provision by taking care of customer services requests/inquiries, as well as the complaints.

Determining and handling employee requirements. Recruit or source the candidates as per the requirements. Screen and select the most appropriate candidates. Take care of the newly hired and re-hired employees. Maintain records of information for all applicants.
Defining a roadmap to meet customer expectations while considering how it will affect the business.

processes.process_name: Evaluate environmental impact of products, services, and operations
processes.description: Evaluating the impact of offerings and the auxiliary operations required to process them on the immediate ecosystem and the environment at large. Study the lifecycle of the products/services offered by the organization. Estimate any affect on the environment through metrics such as a calculation of carbon footprint.
Conducting programs such as on-the-job training sessions, group training workshops, and online training.

Assigning post-sales policies and paying claims on purchased products.  This is a process that is an administrative function focused on creating rules (claim codes). This group ensures that claims are valid and are processed quickly.  As well as to quickly determine responsibility for claim settlement.

processes.process_name: Select partnerships and relationships to support the extended enterprise
processes.description: Supporting the design, manufacture and distribution of product and services through the extended enterprise model.  This is concerned with the strategic decisions on make vs buy, in house or out sourced.  Senior Executives map out how they want to run their business.  Make strategic choices as to whether to buy in components / sub-assemblies, run their own distribution fleet or contract out, own their dealerships or franchise out, etc.  Strategize with partnerships. Collaborate design consideration at strategy level for automotive and procurement act within the Target Operating Model set at strategy level.

Determining different stages of the planning process and accounting. Classify, determine, analyze, interpret, and communicate information to make up-to-date business decisions for better management and control functions.
Managing accounts for large funds-invested projects. Manage and account for fixed assets projects (capital projects), which required significant capital investments over many years.
Creating a story of the customer's experience: from initial contact, through the process of engagement and into a long-term relationship. The goal is to teach organization about the customer.
Comparing revenue targets to reality. Review all transactions and entries passed in final accounts in a year in order to examine profits.

processes.process_name: Process accounts payable and expense reimbursements
processes.description: Handling bills and reimbursements to be made. Make payments for goods or services taken or used on behalf of the organization.

Managing cash collections and disbursements made by operating units across the enterprise. When appropriate, transfer cash from the operating units to parent-level bank accounts managed by the organization's treasury team.

Managing business's investments in trading in bonds, currencies, financial derivatives, etc. Manage the financial assets and holdings of the organization. Optimize the organization's liquidity. Invest excess cash. Reduce financial risks.
Estimating the organization's periodic tax liabilities. Ensure that appropriate taxing authorities receive tax return filings and payments when due.
Making and collecting payments for transactions in products/services, and transporting them to interested markets.

Defining a plan that removes customer obstacles by gathering operational insight and competitive insight, as well as improving soft skills and forward resolution for employees. Develop customer segmentation. Define rules and regulations for customer service. Establish service levels for customers.

processes.process_name: Develop and manage IT customer relationships
processes.description: Creating and administering relationships with IT customers. Understanding customer needs including high-level business requirements for IT transformation. Plan for and communicate IT services along with establishing IT service levels, providing transformation guidance, and performance analysis that foster IT customer relationships.

processes.process_name: Develop and manage IT resilience and risk
processes.description: Develop and include the processes required to rapidly adapt and respond to any internal or external opportunity, demand, disruption, or threat to IT and cybersecurity. Build a dynamic, strategic, and integrated approach to managing IT and cyber risks, compliance obligations, and resilience, while ensuring alignment with global standards and frameworks.

Establishing and managing services for providing support to users of IT services and solutions. Define the plethora of services by which the organization assists users of computers, software products, or other information technology products.
Determining the impacts of environmental health and safety. Create and implement the EHS program. Train and educate employees of the EHS function. Oversee and manage the EHS program.

Administering internal controls. This process requires the organization to manage entity's board of trustees, management, and other personnel in order to offer judicious assurance about the achievement of effectiveness, proficiency of operations, and reliability of financial reporting.
Managing steps to confirm enduring compliance to industry regulations and government legislation.

Managing organizational attributes that are closely associated with the quality of output. Determine the quality requirements. Evaluate the correspondence between the quality performance and requirements. Manage non-conformance activities. Ensure implementation and maintenance of the enterprise quality management system.
Creating new and improving existing analytical capabilities to enhance data management pipeline.

Storing, managing, curating and delivering enterprise content and knowledge assets to enable consistent reuse and informed decision making.  Establish structures and governance that support classification, semantic enrichment, and lifecycle management of content across formats and repositories.  This includes all forms of emerging technologies such as artificial intelligence (AI), machine learning assisted tagging, automated classification, and semantic content processing.
Planning, designing, and implementing the change. Ensure improvement in the change process.

Assessing all forces, entities, and systems that are external to an organization but can affect its operation. Analyze far-reaching currents in the macroeconomic situation, assess the competition, evaluate technological changes, and identify societal as well as ecological issues of concern. Create a big-picture understanding of externalities, with sufficient depth across individual aspects.
Conveying planned procedures and methods to both internal departments and external stakeholders like customers, suppliers, etc., in an effective manner based on organizational objective.

Selecting relevant projects of strategic significance that create opportunities for the organization to realize its long-term objectives, on the basis of their suitability to the organization's constraints and reality. Select from the process Evaluate strategic initiatives [10058], based on their applicability and feasibility for the organization. Enlist senior management, especially strategy personnel.

Designing and constructing assets such as machines, tools, factories, etc. Manage steps to acquire assets including managing capital, as well as planning, scheduling, and overseeing acquisition/construction.

Managing the disposition of assets at their end-of-life. End-of-life for an asset may be due to obsolescence, replacement, excess capacity, or disrepair among other potential factors. Steps may include decommissioning, disassembly, recycling, etc. Tracking and reporting may also be appropriate for some or all asset types due to law, regulation, or social/environmental responsibility.
Planning, acquiring, and managing facilities, workspaces, and supporting assets. Acquire, configure, and manage facilities and workspaces, to include supporting equipment and materials.

processes.process_name: Develop and manage enterprise-wide knowledge management (KM) capability
processes.description: Creating and administering the capability of the organization's knowledge management function. Develop a strategy for knowledge management. Assess capabilities of the knowledge management function.
Defining and managing measurement and benchmarking. Measure and benchmark the performance of internal processes, as well as the organization as a whole.

processes.process_name: Review effectiveness of supply chain and distribution network
processes.description: Determining the performance of supply chain to all departments and logistics from input to shop floor. Seeking performance reviews at each intersection and communication channels. Review effectiveness of supply chain and distribution to check if it is meeting the demands of the various groups and organizations that are concerned with its activities (groups might include customers, partners, suppliers, and vendors).

Arranging and leading meetings, seminars, workshops and training events with customers to educate them about current offerings, best practices and technological advances to provide more value to customers and to increase their attrition and loyalty.

Developing and managing sustainability practices for the organization. Ensure proper understanding and communication of ESG standards, requirements, capabilities, and future trends. Promote awareness, alignment, and continuity.

Establishing guidelines for how resources engage with the customer. For example, set rules of accountability, interaction, and accommodation when engaging the customer. Resources should be polite, empathetic, and attentive.
Execution of sales in an online environment.

Maintaining master data of finished products and inventory. Identify the requirements of finished products at the destination, as well as partner requirements. Calculate the consolidation at source. Manage replenishment planning. Create and administer a dispatch plan. Calculate load plans for destinations and partners. Manage the cost of supplying these products. Ensure effective utilization of capacity.

Appraising market opportunities by quantifying and subjecting them to prioritization, as well as validation tests. Closely examine the market opportunities that have been identified by Perform customer and market intelligence analysis [10106]. Triangulate those opportunities to capitalize by finding a fit between identified opportunities and the composite of organizational capabilities and business strategy.

Defining and overseeing the positioning, value proposition, and governance of brands to ensure a consistent identity, clear differentiation, and alignment with overall marketing direction and business objectives across markets and offerings.

Establishing all the activities needed to identify the appropriate channels to market to different customer segments as defined in Determine target segments [10117]. This involves finding channel partners, ensuring that the channels align with organizational strategy for each segment, and the final channel selection process.

Conceptualizing, testing, and executing product/service/brand promotions. Once a promotion has launched, this process continues as the organization tweaks parts of the promotion or chooses to use ideas or lessons learned during the promotion in future activities. The promotion's performance according to organizational measures is also evaluated in this process. Determine early on whether you need third party help with promotion. Purchase lists, consult with social media experts, hire seasonal staff, or pay for additional research.
Creating descriptions of products that are promotional and informative in content in order to initiate and increase sales. Marketing content consists of text, and optionally, images.

Establishing specific quantitative and qualitative measures of realizing sales targets. Create sales targets by analyzing historical sales data and comparing the forecasts to results, in light of customer and market intelligence. Examine the performance of sales personnel in light of market opportunities. Based on this review, establish sales targets along with metrics to quantify these goals, corresponding with the overall business strategy.

Creating strategies for production processes, as well as the process of managing materials. Define production and supply constraints. Design a blueprint of the workplace. Establish rules and regulations regarding the employees, outsourcing of services, and the expenditure to be incurred on the manufacturing capital.

processes.process_name: Maintain production records and manage lot traceability
processes.description: Perpetuating the production records by systematically documenting and using it to ensure the effective management of lots. Determine the lot numbering system and its use. (The lot number enables tracking of the constituent parts, as well as labor and equipment records involved in the manufacturing of a product. It enables manufacturers and to perform quality control checks, calculate expiration dates, and issue corrections of their production output.)

Scheduling additional investigative field service. This is performed for high priority claims or claims that require additional investigation. Field service engineers will gather additional information, perform further investigation, and qualify the definition of the issue.

processes.process_name: Identify incomplete service orders and service failures
processes.description: Determining orders which have not been completed or delivered. Identify the service orders that are partially or entirely incomplete, as well as the orders that have not been delivered to the customer. Use techniques such as project trackers to recognize the progress of the service orders.

Creating and deploying an architecture for securing the changes deployed in the organization. Create and develop protocols that ensure proper and efficient use of deployed IT services and solutions. Test, evaluate, and implement the policies and protocols.

Communicating how customer service interactions are handled including what is expected when engaging the customer. Relate service level expectations to the workforce. Ensure positive customer experience.

processes.process_name: Define and manage customer service channel strategy
processes.description: Define the channels and communication methods that will be used to deliver customer service, including phone, email, chat, social media, and in-person interactions.

processes.process_name: Define customer service policies and procedures
processes.description: Develop policies and procedures for delivering customer service, including handling customer complaints, resolving issues, and maintaining customer records.

Creating the architecture for the IT services and solutions. Assess architecture and business constraints in order to understand integration requirements. Promote existing architecture. Manage exceptions.

processes.process_name: Plan and manage service delivery control
processes.description: Determine and manage service delivery flow across different business functions. Understand the level of services needed by different stakeholders. Identify major service delivery touch points and criticality associated. Ensure timely communication with users.
Creating and providing funds for necessary adjustments and deductions, including all expenses that were required for the business at certain point in time.
Determining the needs for internal resources and vacancies.

processes.process_name: Establish wages, salaries, and benefits strategy
processes.description: Defining the strategic approach for wages, salaries, and benefits to support workforce attraction, retention, performance, and alignment with organizational objectives and market conditions.
Identifying and resolving internal needs/inquiries for service/solution that cannot be resolved immediately. Research inquiries that require the need of exceptional solutions.

Administering the efforts and activities for IT service/solution remediation. This process element requires the organization to create plans for corrective action in collaboration with government agencies and pertinent professional services agencies which specialize in remediation efforts relevant to the organization's service/solution. Additionally, the organization needs to consult experts to validate the plan, determine resources allocation, resolve any legal concerns, and formulate a company-wide policy for IT service/solution remediation.

processes.process_name: Determine foreign exchange hedge requirements in accordance with risk policy
processes.description: Deciding the requirements on investments in foreign exchange made by trading in futures or options market, on the basis of current risk policy.

Devising business plans and procedures for manufacturing/operations/production and delivery of services offered by the organization. Further in general terms the total amount of output that the manufacturing department is responsible to produce for each period.

processes.process_name: Develop and implement workforce planning, policies, and strategies
processes.description: Creating and executing strategies and policies for smooth administration of workforce. Determine and gather skill requirements. Plan the requirements for employee resourcing per unit. Create compensation, succession, HR program, and employee diversity plans. Develop and administer policies for HR. Develop benefits for employees. Create models for work force strategies.
Implementing the communication plan for employees. Initiate dialogues and engagement by monitoring the exchange of ideas and opinions, the development of personal relationships, etc.

Evaluating quality performance through periodic or episodic testing against the established standards for quality characteristics. For periodic testing, design a schedule with sufficient time to make any required adjustments to the process or system to maintain the desired level of quality. For episodic testing, conduct a test whenever a known non-conformance or fault occurs, which results in outputs or outcomes known to be unsatisfactory to performance requirements.

processes.process_name: Test market for new or revised products and services
processes.description: Expanding on the marketplace analysis that took place earlier in the product development lifecycle by testing the market against offerings. The results from this in-depth analysis will help the organization finalize product/service characteristics and technical requirements and also identify any needed changes in the manufacturing and delivery processes that support market delivery. To prepare a detailed market study that accounts for any changes in the global environment, the organization may want to conduct a series of interviews, workshops, and focus groups with potential and existing customers.

processes.process_name: Measure customer satisfaction with customer problems, requests, and inquiries handling
processes.description: Calculating satisfaction levels of customers by effectively evaluating the process of handling requests/inquiries of customers. Effectively calculate the performance of customer-requests/inquiries handling and resolution. Obtain information regarding requests/inquiries handling and resolution through customer feedback. Use it to explore new ideas and opportunities for enhanced customer requests/inquiries handling and resolution process.
Awareness of the employee legislature that is in place for the organization.  The regulatory environment could include areas, regions, countries, or technologies (around AI, for example).

processes.process_name: Develop and manage reward, recognition, and motivation programs
processes.description: Developing a salary/compensation structure and plan; developing a benefits and reward plan; develop commission plan; performing competitive analyses of benefits and rewards; identifying compensation requirements based on compensation, benefits, and HR policies; administering compensation, commission, and rewards to employees; and rewarding and motivating employees.

Understanding the necessity of IT transformation for the business. This is inclusive of all forms of new and evolving technology such as artificial intelligence (AI). Collect and analyze customer requirements. Identify opportunities and prioritize outcomes. Develop and support business case for transformation. Develop transformation plan and roadmap.

Outline and manage the innovation of technology within the organization. This is inclusive of all forms of new and evolving technology such as artificial intelligence (AI). Research and understand emerging future technological concepts and capabilities. Plan for IT innovation investments. Plan and execute viable innovation projects.
